title: 正德十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
山西鄉試錄序
我
朝三歲取士著爲定制行之百
有餘年條式品格愈嚴愈密
奉行之者公明正大之意視
初始猶一〔日〕也法久而無弊
者莫善于是乃今正德十四
===
年已卯復當其期于
皇上爲五開科而歲星亦一周矣
山西布政使司復舉行之如
制而巡按御史周〔宣〕寔監臨
焉先是御史孫〔孟和〕敦維盛
典禮聘〔淮〕等以司考校鎮守
太監吳〔經〕夙在地方特重文
punctuated:
山西鄉試錄序

我朝三歲取士，著爲定制，行之百有餘年，條式品格愈嚴愈密。奉行之者公明正大之意，視初始猶一〔日〕也。法久而無弊者，莫善于是。乃今正德十四年已卯，復當其期，于皇上爲五開科，而歲星亦一周矣。山西布政使司復舉行之如制，而巡按御史周〔宣〕寔監臨焉。先是，御史孫〔孟和〕敦維盛典，禮聘〔淮〕等以司考校。鎮守太監吳〔經〕夙在地方，特重文
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Shanxi Provincial Examination

Our dynasty established the selection of scholars every three years as a fixed institution and has practiced it for more than a hundred years. Its regulations and standards have become ever stricter and more exacting. Those who administer it retain the same spirit of impartiality, discernment, uprightness, and fairness as at its inception. Among institutions that have endured without developing abuses, none surpasses this one. Now, in the fourteenth year of Zhengde, the jimao year [1519; cyclical designation transcribed doubtfully], the appointed time has come again. This is the fifth examination held under His Majesty, and Jupiter has also completed one circuit. The Shanxi Provincial Administration Commission again conducted it according to the established regulations, with Regional Inspector Zhou Xuan serving as Supervising Official. Earlier, Censor Sun Menghe, earnestly upholding this grand institution, had ceremonially invited Huai and others to oversee the examination and assessment. The Grand Defender, Eunuch Director Wu Jing, had long been stationed in the region and placed particular esteem upon literary …

title: 正德十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
儒巡撫都御史張〔禬志 學〕
清戎御史甯〔欽洛〕任鹽法御
史宋〔鉞〕先後風厲士氣益振
戶部員外郎王〔濟〕行人鄧〔繼
曾〕
龐〔淳〕亦各以使事至樂觀
厥成至期啓院御史周〔宣〕集
提調左布政使胡〔玥〕右布政
===
使汪〔獲麟〕監試按察使張〔璉〕
僉事田〔汝耔〕考試官〔淮〕教諭
成〔世安〕同考試官教諭王〔輔〕
〔臣〕王〔文昌〕貫埼訓導呂〔端〕彭
〔祥〕張〔經〕齊肅以入防範於外
則以屬左參政劉〔澤〕右參政
昭〕
石〔昭〕左參議王〔承祥〕右參議
punctuated: 儒。巡撫都御史張〔禬志 學〕、清戎御史甯〔欽洛〕、任鹽法御史宋〔鉞〕先後風厲，士氣益振。戶部員外郎王〔濟〕、行人鄧〔繼曾〕、龐〔淳〕亦各以使事至，樂觀厥成。至期啓院，御史周〔宣〕集提調左布政使胡〔玥〕、右布政使汪〔獲麟〕、監試按察使張〔璉〕、僉事田〔汝耔〕、考試官〔淮〕、教諭成〔世安〕、同考試官教諭王〔輔〕〔臣〕、王〔文昌〕、貫埼、訓導呂〔端〕、彭〔祥〕、張〔經〕，齊肅以入。防範於外，則以屬左參政劉〔澤〕、右參政昭〕石〔昭〕、左參議王〔承祥〕、右參議
translation_en:
…Confucian scholars. The Grand Coordinator and Censor-in-chief Zhang〔Huizhi Xue [?]〕, the Censor for Military Reorganization Ning〔Qinluo [?]〕, and the Censor responsible for the Salt Administration Song〔Yue〕successively encouraged and exhorted the scholars, whose morale rose still further. Wang Ji, Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue, and the Messengers Deng Jizeng and Pang Chun also arrived on their respective official missions and were pleased to witness the examination’s successful completion.

When the appointed time came and the examination compound was opened, Censor Zhou Xuan assembled the Proctors, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Hu Yue and Right Provincial Administration Commissioner Wang Huolin; the examination monitors, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner Zhang Lian and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Tian Ruzi; the Examiners, Huai and Instructor Cheng Shi’an; and the Associate Examiners, Instructors Wang Fuchen [?], Wang Wenchang, and Guan Qi, and Assistant Instructors Lü Duan, Peng Xiang, and Zhang Jing. They entered together in solemn order. Responsibility for security outside was entrusted to Left Administration Vice Commissioner Liu Ze, Right Administration Vice Commissioner Shi Zhao [the transcription repeats part of the name here: ?], Left Administration Assistant Commissioner Wang Chengxiang, and the Right Administration Assistant Commissioner…

title: 正德十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
汪〔正京〕副使沙〔鵬〕僉事尹〔金〕
〔鯉〕潘〔選〕盛〔鵬〕暨都指揮陳〔謹〕
袁〔勛〕劉〔漢〕乃合提學副使馬
〔卿〕所甄拔三府五州士而三
試之封局圍棘樹簾隔座糊
名易書按經彙考限日分場
咸如制其法維舊其事維新
===
閱二十日事竣揭榜于通衢
刻其文之合式者二十篇第
其名之中式者六十有五人
與諸執事諸條格爲試錄夫
榜以曉近其事略錄以傳遠
其體詳故宜有序而〔淮〕以職
事序諸首昔人有言長材大
punctuated:
汪〔正京〕、副使沙〔鵬〕、僉事尹〔金〕〔鯉〕、潘〔選〕、盛〔鵬〕，暨都指揮陳〔謹〕、袁〔勛〕、劉〔漢〕。乃合提學副使馬〔卿〕所甄拔三府五州士，而三試之。封局圍棘，樹簾隔座，糊名易書，按經彙考，限日分場，咸如制。其法維舊，其事維新。
閱二十日，事竣，揭榜于通衢，刻其文之合式者二十篇，第其名之中式者六十有五人，與諸執事、諸條格爲試錄。夫榜以曉近，其事略；錄以傳遠，其體詳。故宜有序，而〔淮〕以職事序諸首。昔人有言：「長材大
translation_en:
…Wang Zhengjing; Surveillance Vice Commissioner Sha Peng; Assistant Surveillance Commissioners Yin Jinli, Pan Xuan, and Sheng Peng; together with Regional Military Commissioners Chen Jin, Yuan Xun, and Liu Han. We then assembled the scholars from the three prefectures and five subprefectures whom Ma Qing, Surveillance Vice Commissioner for Education, had selected, and examined them in three sessions. The examination compound was sealed and enclosed with thorn barriers; curtains were erected to separate the seats; candidates’ names were concealed and their scripts recopied; papers were grouped and assessed according to their respective Classics; and the sessions were held on appointed days. Everything followed the regulations. The procedures were inherited from the past; their implementation was renewed on this occasion.
After twenty days, the work was completed, and the results were posted on a main thoroughfare. Twenty essays that met the prescribed standards were printed, and the names of the sixty-five successful candidates were listed in rank order. These, together with the names of the examination personnel and the regulations, formed the examination record. The posted list informs those nearby and gives only a brief account; the record transmits the proceedings to distant places and provides fuller detail. It therefore fittingly has a preface, and I, Huai, by virtue of my duties, have placed this preface at its beginning. Someone in former times said: “Outstanding talents and great …

title: 正德十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
䶂往往出於西北蓋以文章
望東南也今玆之來履方輿
之雄勝固未暇接觀其人品
而得先從事於所謂文章焉
者窮日夜之力因所疑而致
志焉口誦目披則藻繢絢爛
之所照映和豈沉渾之所宣
===
颺使人起敬而忘食已恨於
不能盡錄而錄之止於是者
固當嘗一臠而知鼎矣持此
以往其於吳蜀豈獨異哉然
後歎古人名理之未盡也蓋
自古帝王之都多在西北而
都於山之西者為盛惟我
punctuated: 䶂往往出於西北，蓋以文章望東南也。今玆之來，履方輿之雄勝，固未暇接觀其人品，而得先從事於所謂文章焉者。窮日夜之力，因所疑而致志焉。口誦目披，則藻繢絢爛之所照映，和豈沉渾之所宣颺，使人起敬而忘食。已恨於不能盡錄，而錄之止於是者，固當嘗一臠而知鼎矣。持此以往，其於吳蜀豈獨異哉？然後歎古人名理之未盡也。蓋自古帝王之都多在西北，而都於山之西者為盛。惟我
translation_en: …[?] often emerge from the northwest; in literary composition, however, one presumably looks to the southeast. Coming here on this occasion, I have traversed this magnificent terrain. Although I have not yet had leisure to meet its people and observe their character, I have first been able to engage with what is called their literary composition. Exerting myself day and night, I concentrated my attention wherever doubts arose. Reading aloud and examining the texts, I found their brilliant literary ornament illuminating the page, and their harmony, joy, depth, and fullness [?] finding expression. They inspired reverence and made me forget to eat. I already regretted being unable to record them all; yet, though the selections recorded extend only this far, one should surely be able to judge the contents of the cauldron by tasting a single morsel. Taking these as evidence, how could this region stand apart from Wu and Shu in literary achievement? Only then did I lament that the ancients’ celebrated judgments had not exhausted the truth. Since antiquity, imperial capitals have mostly been in the northwest, and those established in Shanxi were especially flourishing. Our own …

title: 正德十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
聖祖龍飛淮甸奄有區夏而混一
之
文皇作京密邇三晉
列聖繼承重熙累洽佑啓文明鼓
舞感孚之妙先及厚被旋斡
化工所謂道德齊而風俗一
車同軌而書同文者正其時
===
也尚何有於南北東西之云
乎然後知古人之局於所見
而不見
今日之全盛者爲陋也夫材器
質也文章文也山西之士不
改昔人之所長而兼有往時
之所未備其皆彬彬然中行
punctuated: 聖祖龍飛淮甸，奄有區夏而混一之。文皇作京，密邇三晉。列聖繼承，重熙累洽，佑啓文明，鼓舞感孚之妙，先及厚被，旋斡化工。所謂道德齊而風俗一，車同軌而書同文者，正其時也。尚何有於南北東西之云乎？然後知古人之局於所見，而不見今日之全盛者爲陋也。夫材器，質也；文章，文也。山西之士不改昔人之所長，而兼有往時之所未備，其皆彬彬然中行
translation_en: …the sagely founder rose like a dragon in the Huai region, gained possession of the Chinese realm, and united it. Emperor Wen established the capital close to the Three Jin regions. Successive sage emperors carried on their legacy, adding prosperity to prosperity and peace to peace, fostering and advancing cultural refinement. Their wondrous power to inspire, move, and win allegiance reached this region early and blessed it abundantly, directing the work of transformation. This is precisely the age described in the saying: “Moral principles are uniform and customs united; carriages have the same axle gauge, and writing uses the same script.” What grounds remain, then, for speaking of distinctions between south, north, east, and west? Only then do we recognize the narrowness of the ancients, confined to what they had seen and unable to witness the fullness of prosperity today. Talent and capacity constitute substance; literary accomplishment constitutes refinement. The scholars of Shanxi retain the strengths of their predecessors while also possessing what earlier times lacked. Are they not all harmoniously combining substance and refinement, following the balanced course…

title: 正德十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
之士矣乎孔子猶以不得中
行為恨而此六十五人信乃
中行之士矣有非中行之士
矣乎主司者於是乎不知言
矣雖然質本乎性文成乎學
學所以文其質也諸士子勿
徒曰藉此以仕而已矣則是
===
榮華利祿之資爾又安貴於
文章為哉嗚呼知山西之文
章者主司也能使山西之文
章重於他日者諸士子也非
主司也可不慎哉
湖廣黃州府儒學教授喻淮
謹序
punctuated:
之士矣乎？孔子猶以不得中行為恨，而此六十五人信乃中行之士矣。有非中行之士矣乎？主司者於是乎不知言矣。雖然，質本乎性，文成乎學，學所以文其質也。諸士子勿徒曰藉此以仕而已矣，則是榮華利祿之資爾，又安貴於文章為哉？嗚呼！知山西之文章者，主司也；能使山西之文章重於他日者，諸士子也，非主司也。可不慎哉？
湖廣黃州府儒學教授喻淮謹序。
translation_en:
…men who follow the mean? Even Confucius regretted being unable to find men who followed the mean, yet these sixty-five men surely are such men. Could any among them fail to follow the mean? If so, the officials presiding over the examination would have shown themselves unable to discern men through their words.
Nevertheless, substance is rooted in one's nature, while refinement is achieved through learning: learning is what refines one's substance. You candidates must not merely say that you will use this to enter official service and nothing more. That would make it merely a means to splendor, profit, and emolument; what value would literary accomplishment then have? Alas! Those who recognize Shanxi's literary accomplishment are the presiding officials; those who can bring greater esteem to Shanxi's literary accomplishment in days to come are you candidates, not the presiding officials. Can you afford to be heedless?
Preface respectfully composed by Yu Huai, Instructor at the Confucian School of Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang.

punctuated:
正德十四年山西鄉試。

監臨官：巡按山西監察御史周宣〔彥通，福建莆田縣人，乙丑進士〕。

提調官：山西等處承宣布政使司左布政使胡玥〔朝重，湖廣襄陽衛人，己未進士〕。山西等處承宣布政使司右布政使汪獲麟〔仁甫，騰驤左衛籍，浙江山陰縣人，癸丑進士〕。

監試官：山西等處提刑按察司按察使張璉〔汝器，陝西耀州人，壬戌進士〕。山西等處提刑按察司僉事田汝耔〔勤甫，河南祥符縣人，乙丑進士〕。

考試官：湖廣黃州府儒學教授喻淮〔東之，廣西臨桂縣人，乙卯貢士〕。江西饒州府鄱陽縣儒學教諭成世安〔邦正，湖廣藍山縣人，甲子貢士〕。

同考試官：直隸蘇州府吳縣儒學教諭王輔臣〔元忠，河南陳留縣人，癸酉貢士〕。直隸松江府華亭縣儒學教諭王文昌〔道亨，順天府平谷縣人，丁卯貢士〕。直隸廬州府舒城縣儒學教諭賈琦〔希韓，山東濟寧衛籍，順天府密雲縣人，丙子貢士〕。直隸揚州府高郵州儒學訓導彭祥〔秉瑞，河南光山縣人，庚午貢士〕。直隸大名府開州長垣縣儒學訓導呂端〔正夫，山東濮州人，庚午貢士〕。
translation_en:
Shanxi Provincial Examination, fourteenth year of Zhengde (1519).

Supervising Official:
Zhou Xuan, Investigating Censor touring Shanxi. His courtesy name was Yantong; he was from Putian County, Fujian, and was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the yichou year.

Proctors:
Hu Yue, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Shanxi. His courtesy name was Chaozhong; he was from Xiangyang Guard, Huguang, and was a metropolitan graduate of the jiwei year.
Wang Huolin, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner of Shanxi. His courtesy name was Renfu; he was registered with Tengxiang Left Guard and was a native of Shanyin County, Zhejiang. He was a metropolitan graduate of the guichou year.

Examination Overseers:
Zhang Lian, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner of Shanxi. His courtesy name was Ruqi; he was from Yaozhou, Shaanxi, and was a metropolitan graduate of the renxu year.
Tian Ruzi, Assistant Provincial Surveillance Commissioner of Shanxi. His courtesy name was Qinfu; he was from Xiangfu County, Henan, and was a metropolitan graduate of the yichou year.

Examiners:
Yu Huai, Professor at the Confucian School of Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang. His courtesy name was Dongzhi; he was from Lingui County, Guangxi, and was a tribute student (gongshi) of the yimao year.
Cheng Shi’an, Instructor at the Confucian School of Poyang County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi. His courtesy name was Bangzheng; he was from Lanshan County, Huguang, and was a tribute student of the jiazi year.

Associate Examiners:
Wang Fuchen, Instructor at the Confucian School of Wu County, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili. His courtesy name was Yuanzhong; he was from Chenliu County, Henan, and was a tribute student of the guiyou year.
Wang Wenchang, Instructor at the Confucian School of Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, Zhili. His courtesy name was Daoheng; he was from Pinggu County, Shuntian Prefecture, and was a tribute student of the dingmao year.
Jia Qi, Instructor at the Confucian School of Shucheng County, Luzhou Prefecture, Zhili. His courtesy name was Xihan; he was registered with Jining Guard, Shandong, and was a native of Miyun County, Shuntian Prefecture. He was a tribute student of the bingzi year.
Peng Xiang, Assistant Instructor at the Confucian School of Gaoyou Subprefecture, Yangzhou Prefecture, Zhili. His courtesy name was Bingrui; he was from Guangshan County, Henan, and was a tribute student of the gengwu year.
Lü Duan, Assistant Instructor at the Confucian School of Changyuan County, Kaizhou Subprefecture, Daming Prefecture, Zhili. His courtesy name was Zhengfu; he was from Puzhou, Shandong, and was a tribute student of the gengwu year.

title: 正德十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
直隸大名府滑縣儒學訓導張經〔大倫陜西汧陽縣人　庚午貢士〕
印卷官
山西等處承宣布政使司經歷司都事藺天倫〔理夫山東德平縣人　監生〕
山西等處提刑按察司經歷司經歷吳瑄〔汝璋遼東前屯衛人　監生〕

受卷官
平陽府蒲州知州王俊民〔用章湖廣石首縣人　甲戌進士〕

title: 正德十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
因民之所利而利之斯不亦惠而不費乎
故君子尊德性而道問學致廣大而盡精
微極高明而道中庸温故而知新敦厚
以崇禮
孟子曰許子必種粟而後食乎曰然許子
必織布而後衣乎曰否許子衣褐許子
冠乎曰冠曰奚冠曰冠素曰自織之與
曰否以粟易之曰許子奚爲不自織曰
害於耕曰許子以釜甑爨以鐵耕乎曰
然自爲之與曰否以粟易之
===
易
貞固足以幹事
王假之尚大也勿憂宜日中宜照天下也
夫易開物成務冒天下之道如斯而已者
也
物畜然後有禮故受之以履履而泰然後

因民之所利而利之，斯不亦惠而不費乎？

故君子尊德性而道問學，致廣大而盡精微，極高明而道中庸，温故而知新，敦厚以崇禮。

孟子曰：「許子必種粟而後食乎？」曰：「然。」「許子必織布而後衣乎？」曰：「否，許子衣褐。」「許子冠乎？」曰：「冠。」曰：「奚冠？」曰：「冠素。」曰：「自織之與？」曰：「否，以粟易之。」曰：「許子奚爲不自織？」曰：「害於耕。」曰：「許子以釜甑爨，以鐵耕乎？」曰：「然。」「自爲之與？」曰：「否，以粟易之。」

易

貞固足以幹事。

王假之，尚大也；勿憂，宜日中，宜照天下也。

夫易，開物成務，冒天下之道，如斯而已者也。

物畜然後有禮，故受之以履；履而泰，然後
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

By benefiting the people through what they themselves find beneficial, is one not generous without incurring expense?

Thus the gentleman honors his moral nature and pursues inquiry and learning. He reaches the broad and great while exhausting the subtle and minute; he attains the lofty and luminous while following the Mean. He reviews the old to understand the new, and deepens his sincerity and generosity to exalt ritual propriety.

Mencius said, “Must Master Xu grow grain before he eats?” The reply was, “Yes.” “Must Master Xu weave cloth before he dresses?” The reply was, “No. Master Xu wears coarse cloth.” “Does Master Xu wear a cap?” The reply was, “He does.” Mencius asked, “What kind of cap?” The reply was, “A cap of plain silk.” He asked, “Does he weave it himself?” The reply was, “No. He exchanges grain for it.” He asked, “Why does Master Xu not weave it himself?” The reply was, “It would interfere with his farming.” He asked, “Does Master Xu cook with pots and steamers and plow with iron implements?” The reply was, “Yes.” “Does he make them himself?” The reply was, “No. He exchanges grain for them.”

Book of Changes

Steadfastness and firmness suffice to manage affairs.

“The king attains it” means that he esteems greatness. “Do not worry; be like the sun at noon” means that he should illuminate all under Heaven.

The Changes discloses things, brings undertakings to completion, and encompasses the Way of all under Heaven. It amounts simply to this.

Only after things have been gathered together is there ritual propriety; therefore, Xu (Accumulation) is followed by Lü (Treading). Through treading comes tranquillity, and only then…

Book of Documents

…at peace; therefore it is followed by Tai (Peace). [This continues the preceding page’s passage from the Book of Changes; the heading “Book of Documents” appears before it in the transcription.]

Be settled in your proper place. Attend to the slightest beginnings and to secure repose; let those who assist you be upright. Whenever you act, respond fully to the aspirations of those who await you.

Thus may you manifestly receive the favor of the Lord on High; Heaven will renew its mandate with blessings.

If I am making a well-seasoned broth, you shall be its salt and sour plums.

Reaffirm the boundaries of the suburban territories; carefully secure the borders and their defenses, so as to bring peace to all within the Four Seas.

Examine and judge these matters carefully! Where any of the five punishments is doubtful, there is provision for pardon; where any of the five fines is doubtful, there is provision for remission. Examine and judge these matters carefully!

Book of Odes

In the days of the third month, we attend to our plowshares; in the days of the fourth, we set our feet to work. Together with our wives and children, we take food to those southern fields. The field overseer arrives and is pleased.

The lord has arrived; we gaze upon his dragon banner.

Ah, how harmonious the drums and bells! Ah, how joyful the Biyong ceremonial hall! The alligator-hide drums resound; the blind musicians perform their work.

He receives small and large jade tokens and becomes the rallying point of the states below, bearing Heaven’s blessings. Neither contentious nor impetuous, neither hard nor yielding, he administers government with generous ease, and all blessings converge upon him. He receives small and great offerings and becomes the mighty support of the states below, bearing Heaven’s favor. He displays his valor, neither shaken nor swayed, neither fearful nor alarmed; all blessings gather around him.

Spring and Autumn Annals

Five policy questions.
Question: The Six Classics all record how emperors and kings governed, but none bears more directly on the essentials than the Book of Documents. As the earlier Confucian scholar Cai Shen said, “The government of emperors and kings is rooted in the Way; the Way of emperors and kings is rooted in the heart.” This is precisely the point. How could those who subsequently discuss government proceed if they abandoned this heart and this Way? Yet since the Han dynasty, many illustrious rulers and righteous sovereigns have devoted themselves to this book. Why, then, have the results of their government fallen short of antiquity? Or…

text:

安内攘外務本節用恤刑救災表忠節

之政者可得而言歟敬天勤民親賢務

===

之抑別有其說歟昔魏相好觀漢興以

太祖高皇帝聰明天縱，聖學日躋，御極以来，講論治道，靡間昕夕。治效之隆，盖已匹休帝王，而陋漢唐宋於下風矣。其在當時，安内攘外、務本節用、恤刑救災、表忠節、厚風俗，皆致治之法也。其有合於帝王之政者，可得而言歟？敬天勤民、親賢務學、崇抑畏、戒逸欲，皆致治之本也。揆之帝王傳心之學，果異世而同符歟？若乃制作之出於宸衷、符章之下於方國、謨訓之傳於子孫者，置之典謨訓誥之間，可以並列而無媿歟？列聖相承，治隆俗美，百有餘年，其皆有得於聖祖家法之傳歟？今日格心之學，將舉此而措之，抑別有其說歟？昔魏相好觀漢興以来故事，范仲淹自爲秀才時，便以天下爲己任。此諸子今日之責也，請終言之，毋讓。

translation_en:
… Emperor Gao, Taizu, was endowed by Heaven with intelligence, and his sagely learning advanced daily. From his accession to the throne, he discussed the Way of governance without pause, morning or evening. His achievements in government surely matched the glory of the ancient emperors and kings, relegating the Han, Tang, and Song to an inferior position. In his time, securing the realm internally and repelling external threats, attending to the fundamental occupation of agriculture and economizing on expenditure, exercising care in punishment and relieving disasters, honoring loyalty and integrity, and enriching customary morality were all methods of achieving good government. Can you explain how these accorded with the government of the ancient emperors and kings? Revering Heaven and diligently caring for the people, drawing close to the worthy and pursuing learning, esteeming humility and reverent caution, and guarding against indolence and desire were all foundations of good government. Measured against the learning transmitted from mind to mind by the ancient emperors and kings, did these indeed tally, despite the difference in ages? As for the institutions devised in his imperial mind, the credentials and documents [?] dispatched to the regions, and the counsels and instructions transmitted to his descendants: could these be placed alongside the Canons, Counsels, Instructions, and Announcements of the Book of Documents without shame?

Successive sage sovereigns have carried on his rule, with flourishing government and admirable customs for more than a hundred years. Have they all benefited from the transmission of the Sagely Ancestor’s dynastic precedents? In practicing today the learning that rectifies the ruler’s mind, should we take these up and put them into effect, or is there another explanation? In former times, Wei Xiang delighted in studying precedents from the founding of the Han onward, and Fan Zhongyan, from his days as a student, took responsibility for all under Heaven upon himself. This is your responsibility today, gentlemen. Please discuss it fully, without holding back.

text:

punctuated: 學聖人，且須學顏子。」而顏子所以善學聖人者何在？又曰：「傳孔子之道者，曾子而已。」而曾子所以傳孔子之學，其實何在？又曰：「曾子以後，子思之傳得其宗。」不知子思之學以何為要？又曰：「至孟子而聖人之道益尊。」而孟子之學以何為主？至有以顏子比湯武，孟子並禹稷，而皆不可不知已。宋稱周子之學淵源精粹，闡發幽秘；程伯淳氏負特立之才，知大學之要；程正叔氏為天民之先覺、聖代之真儒。其稱張子厚氏學有本原，西方宗之；至謂朱子集數子之大成，為中興之豪傑。不知諸子所以為名之實，又奚所安？至謂明道似顏子，伊川似孟子，又以橫渠與孟子比，朱子之功不在孟子下，抑又何説也？夫仰觀先後賢哲，俱底于道，要其造詣之力，果相同乎否也？抑孰於聖人之域殆庶幾乎？諸士子志于聖
translation_en:
…to learn from the sages, one must first learn from Master Yan.” What enabled Master Yan to learn so well from the sages? It is also said: “It was Master Zeng alone who transmitted the Way of Confucius.” What, in substance, enabled Master Zeng to transmit the learning of Confucius? It is also said: “After Master Zeng, Zisi’s transmission grasped its essential principles.” What did Zisi regard as essential in learning? It is also said: “With Mengzi, the Way of the sages became still more exalted.” What did Mengzi take as the central concern of learning? Some have even compared Master Yan to Tang and Wu, and placed Mengzi alongside Yu and Ji. All these comparisons must be understood.

In the Song, Master Zhou’s learning was praised as profound in its sources and pure in its essence, elucidating what was hidden and obscure. Cheng Bochun possessed a talent that set him apart and understood the essentials of the Great Learning. Cheng Zhengshu was one of Heaven’s people who first attained awakening, a true Confucian of a sagely age. Zhang Zihou was praised for learning grounded in fundamental sources, and people of the western region revered him as their master. It was even said that Master Zhu brought the achievements of these several masters to their fullest synthesis and was an outstanding figure in the revival of the Way. On what, then, rested the substantive achievements that won these masters their renown? It is further said that Mingdao resembled Master Yan and Yichuan resembled Mengzi; Hengqu, too, is compared with Mengzi, while Master Zhu’s contributions are held to be no less than Mengzi’s. How are these claims to be explained?

When we look up to the worthy and wise of earlier and later times, all attained the Way. Yet, examining the effort through which they reached their attainments, was it indeed the same or not? And who came closest to the realm of the sages? You examination candidates have set your aspirations upon sagehood…

title: 正德十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
賢久矣試言將何所法以爲入道之方
問大學之道自身心以推之家國天下周
禮則治天下之大經大法而本諸身心
其致一也爲學莫先焉然格物致知爲
初用力之地而亡之周禮亦亡冬官先
王之制遂不可備見矣格致之章朱子
嘗取程子之意以補之不知程子何所
取乎夫孔子之脩春秋也猶闕文焉而
必補之何也漢儒以考工記補冬官之
===
亡夫所載固其事也而疑亦成周之遺
書似不爲過而或乃病焉大學出於戴
記錯簡多矣有釋本末而無始終盖亦
缺焉而末之補周禮或以爲出於戰國
之陰謀則幷其全書可疑也而何有於
一官或又以俱不亡者是必有見也不
知其說可乎夫大學亦堯舜以來相傳
之心法非孔魯之私言周禮唐虞稽古
建官之遺亦非周公之創制若得其要
punctuated:
賢久矣，試言將何所法以爲入道之方？
問：大學之道，自身心以推之家國天下；周禮則治天下之大經大法，而本諸身心，其致一也，爲學莫先焉。然格物致知爲初用力之地，而亡之；周禮亦亡冬官，先王之制遂不可備見矣。格致之章，朱子嘗取程子之意以補之，不知程子何所取乎？夫孔子之脩春秋也，猶闕文焉，而必補之，何也？漢儒以考工記補冬官之亡，夫所載固其事也，而疑亦成周之遺書，似不爲過，而或乃病焉。大學出於戴記，錯簡多矣，有釋本末而無始終，盖亦缺焉，而末之補。周禮或以爲出於戰國之陰謀，則幷其全書可疑也，而何有於一官？或又以俱不亡者，是必有見也，不知其說可乎？夫大學亦堯舜以來相傳之心法，非孔魯之私言；周禮，唐虞稽古建官之遺，亦非周公之創制。若得其要，
translation_en:
…you have long aspired to become sages and worthies. Explain what you would take as your model for entering the Way.

Question: The Way of the Great Learning extends from one’s own person and mind to the family, state, and all under Heaven. The Rites of Zhou sets forth the great principles and laws for governing all under Heaven, yet grounds them in the person and mind. Their ultimate purport is the same; nothing takes precedence over them in learning. Yet investigating things and extending knowledge constitute the initial point of application, and the text concerning them has been lost. The Rites of Zhou likewise lacks the section on the Ministry of Works, so the institutions of the former kings can no longer be seen in their entirety. Zhu Xi once drew upon Master Cheng’s ideas to supply the chapter on investigating things and extending knowledge. But what did Master Cheng draw upon? When Confucius edited the Spring and Autumn Annals, he still left gaps in the text. Why, then, must this gap be filled? Han scholars used the Record of Artificers to supply the missing Ministry of Works section. What it records certainly concerns that ministry’s affairs, and it is presumably also a surviving text of the Zhou dynasty. This would seem unobjectionable, yet some find fault with it. The Great Learning comes from Dai’s Record of Rites and contains many misplaced slips. It explains roots and branches but not beginnings and endings, so here too there is presumably a lacuna, yet it has not been supplied [?]. Some regard the Rites of Zhou as a product of the covert schemes of the Warring States period. If so, the entire book is suspect: why concern oneself with a single ministry? Others maintain that neither text has suffered any loss. They must have some insight, but is their explanation tenable? The Great Learning, after all, also embodies the teaching of the mind transmitted since Yao and Shun; it is no mere personal pronouncement of Confucius of Lu [?]. The Rites of Zhou preserves the legacy of Tang Yao and Yu Shun, who examined antiquity in establishing offices; its institutions were likewise not newly invented by the Duke of Zhou. If one grasps their essentials …

title: 正德十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
則不病於亡也然則所謂要者可得而
聞乎明體適用之學莫過於是諸士子
所嘗究心焉者必有見矣
問人主以論相爲職宰相以正君爲職上
下一體固已三代無論漢稱蕭何定一
代規模壯闗中根本曹參自恬清静不
務變更若稱魏相每進奏言真宰相事
丙吉知審陰陽乃宰相職不知諸公相
業之名果皆在玆否歟唐稱房玄齡善
===
謀杜如晦能斷同心徇國姚崇應變成
務宋璟持正守法協心輔佐然其相業
並名止在是歟宋稱韓琦爲相不動聲
色處事應變范仲淹大厲名節振作士
習至云富弼霜日爭嚴咢鑊不避乃目
歐陽脩爲今之韓愈當時之人一曰韓
范二曰富韓而不及歐陽子者其意何
歟夫徧觀諸代列相大臣其間學術有
淺深器識有大小才行有純疵則人品
punctuated:
則不病於亡也。然則所謂要者，可得而聞乎？明體適用之學，莫過於是。諸士子所嘗究心焉者，必有見矣。

問：人主以論相爲職，宰相以正君爲職，上下一體，固已。三代無論，漢稱蕭何定一代規模，壯闗中根本；曹參自恬清静，不務變更。若稱魏相每進奏言真宰相事，丙吉知審陰陽乃宰相職，不知諸公相業之名，果皆在玆否歟？唐稱房玄齡善謀，杜如晦能斷，同心徇國；姚崇應變成務，宋璟持正守法，協心輔佐。然其相業並名，止在是歟？宋稱韓琦爲相，不動聲色，處事應變；范仲淹大厲名節，振作士習。至云富弼霜日爭嚴，咢鑊不避，乃目歐陽脩爲今之韓愈。當時之人，一曰韓范，二曰富韓，而不及歐陽子者，其意何歟？夫徧觀諸代列相大臣，其間學術有淺深，器識有大小，才行有純疵，則人品
translation_en:
…then its loss need not be a cause for concern. May we therefore hear what this essential point is? Nothing surpasses this as learning that illuminates fundamental principles and applies them appropriately in practice. You candidates, having devoted your attention to these matters, must surely have insights to offer.

Question: The ruler’s duty is to assess chief councilors; the chief councilor’s duty is to rectify the ruler. That those above and below form a single body is assuredly so. Leaving aside the Three Dynasties, in the Han, Xiao He is praised for establishing the framework of a dynasty and strengthening its foundation in Guanzhong; Cao Can for resting content in quietude and not pursuing changes. As for the praise of Wei Xiang—that every memorial he submitted addressed the true business of a chief councilor—and of Bing Ji—that he understood that discerning the workings of yin and yang was a chief councilor’s duty—did the reputations of these men for achievement as chief councilors truly rest entirely on these things? In the Tang, Fang Xuanling is praised for skill in planning and Du Ruhui for decisiveness, both serving the state with one mind; Yao Chong for responding to changing circumstances and accomplishing affairs, and Song Jing for upholding what was right and observing the laws, both assisting the ruler with united purpose. Yet did their achievements and shared renown as chief councilors rest on these things alone? In the Song, Han Qi is praised for handling affairs and responding to changing circumstances as chief councilor without betraying emotion in his voice or expression; Fan Zhongyan for vigorously promoting reputation and integrity and revitalizing the habits of scholars. It is further said that Fu Bi rivaled frost and the sun in sternness [?] and did not shrink from the cauldron of execution [?], while Ouyang Xiu was called the Han Yu of his day. People at the time spoke, first, of ‘Han and Fan,’ and second, of ‘Fu and Han,’ but did not include Master Ouyang: what did they mean by this? Surveying the chief councilors and great ministers of successive dynasties, we find that their learning was shallow or deep, their capacity and discernment great or small, and their talents and conduct unblemished or flawed; thus their personal caliber…

title: 正德十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
見已其功業之建立相去次第則一時
治效隨之不知所謂正君之職果誰其
能盡歟其所遭際亦有遇與不遇者歟
夫其所遇果皆係于天歟人歟諸生明
經博學尚友古人非一日矣願述所聞
以觀所志
問山西古冀方也其土墝瘠故民多貧其
俗勤儉故用僅足然堯舜禹嘗都之田
中而賦上晉以世覇富強聞焉其何道
以致之邪今地闢民聚豈特古之時乎
===
國初因土則賦惟內供
藩封外給邊餉其輸京師留郡縣者蓋鮮焉
視他省爲優矣而又制鹽利以濟之雖
公私美溢爲不過也而近來歲供常祿
度支每缺邊庭小警輙已告乏一有水
旱流殍載途而莫之救官民匱竭一至
於此意者生齒繁而地力日薄歟天災
流行而歲之不易歟抑勤儉衰而惰靡
punctuated:
見已。其功業之建立，相去次第，則一時治效隨之。不知所謂正君之職，果誰其能盡歟？其所遭際，亦有遇與不遇者歟？夫其所遇，果皆係于天歟？人歟？諸生明經博學，尚友古人非一日矣，願述所聞，以觀所志。
問：山西古冀方也。其土墝瘠，故民多貧；其俗勤儉，故用僅足。然堯舜禹嘗都之，田中而賦上，晉以世覇富強聞焉，其何道以致之邪？今地闢民聚，豈特古之時乎？國初因土則賦，惟內供藩封，外給邊餉，其輸京師、留郡縣者蓋鮮焉，視他省爲優矣。而又制鹽利以濟之，雖公私美溢爲不過也。而近來歲供常祿，度支每缺；邊庭小警，輙已告乏；一有水旱，流殍載途，而莫之救。官民匱竭，一至於此，意者生齒繁而地力日薄歟？天災流行而歲之不易歟？抑勤儉衰而惰靡
translation_en:
…become apparent. Their accomplishments differ in degree, and the effectiveness of government in their respective times varies accordingly. Who among them, then, could truly fulfill the duty of setting the ruler right? In the circumstances they encountered, were some favored with opportunities and others denied them? Did those opportunities depend entirely upon Heaven, or upon human action? You candidates have studied the Classics thoroughly, acquired broad learning, and long sought fellowship with the ancients. Please set forth what you have learned, so that your aspirations may be discerned.
Question: Shanxi was anciently the region of Ji. Its soil is hard and barren, so its people are mostly poor; their customs favor diligence and frugality, so their resources barely suffice. Yet Yao, Shun, and Yu once established their capitals there. Its fields ranked in the middle grade, while its tax yield ranked in the upper grade; and Jin was renowned for its hegemony over successive generations, its wealth, and its strength. By what means were these achieved? Today, with land opened to cultivation and the population concentrated here, are conditions merely as they were in antiquity? At the founding of our dynasty, taxes were assessed according to the land, chiefly to support the princely establishments within the province and provide military supplies on the frontier. Little was remitted to the capital or retained by the prefectures and counties. Shanxi was thus treated more favorably than other provinces. Salt revenues were also regulated to supplement its resources, so it would not be excessive to expect abundance in both public and private resources [?]. Recently, however, budgetary resources have repeatedly fallen short of the annual provision for regular stipends. At the slightest alarm on the frontier, shortages are immediately reported. Whenever flood or drought occurs, refugees and the bodies of the starved fill the roads, with no one to relieve them. Officials and commoners alike have been reduced to such utter destitution. Might this be because the population has multiplied while the land’s productivity declines daily? Or because natural disasters recur and the years are difficult? Or has diligence and frugality declined, while idleness and extravagance…

title: 正德十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
衆歟抑侵漁逋負之弊積歟或横征妄
費之無極歟求其故而不得也兹欲有
無變通不加賦而用足羸歛增減不歛
民而備周古有法也其可行否乎抑或
別有道乎夫言利與理財異足國裕民
今日所宜亟講也諸士子四民之秀必
上達經國之務而下悉閭閻之隱矣願
一言之將述以
獻
punctuated: 衆歟？抑侵漁逋負之弊積歟？或横征妄費之無極歟？求其故而不得也。兹欲有無變通，不加賦而用足；羸歛增減，不歛民而備周。古有法也，其可行否乎？抑或別有道乎？夫言利與理財異，足國裕民，今日所宜亟講也。諸士子，四民之秀，必上達經國之務，而下悉閭閻之隱矣。願一言之，將述以獻。
translation_en: …have become widespread? Or have the abuses of extortion and unpaid obligations accumulated? Or is it because arbitrary exactions and reckless expenditure know no bounds? We seek the causes but cannot discover them. Now we wish to redistribute resources between places of abundance and scarcity, so that expenditure can be met without increasing taxes; and to adjust surpluses and collections [?], increasing or reducing them, so that reserves are sufficient without further exactions from the people. Antiquity had methods for this. Can they be put into practice? Or is there another way? Speaking of profit differs from managing public finances. Ensuring sufficient resources for the state and prosperity for the people is a matter that urgently requires discussion today. You candidates, the outstanding members of the four occupations, must surely understand the higher concerns of governing the state as well as the hidden hardships of ordinary households. Please offer your views; I shall set them forth for presentation to the throne.

title: 正德十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
因民之所利而利之斯不亦惠而不費乎
王騰鵬
同考試官訓導張　批〔利民之事甚多數而言之祇見纒繞此作獨隱括無遺至不費處尤說得精切得古〕〔人如斯區區之責塞矣〕
同考試官教諭王　批〔渾厚之文得聖人語意〕
考試官教諭成　批〔說聖人惠民之政辭不煩而意自足可取〕
考試官教授喻　批〔平淡中有隽永之味可佳〕
===
君子與自然之利斯為自然之惠也蓋自然之
利即民之所以為利也於此而與之其為惠也
奚費哉昔夫子荅子張五美之問首及於此謂
夫為政莫先於惠民惠民每難於不費於此有
道焉思治世以大德而因五方之產以利民知
生財有大道而順四時之和以阜物如丘陵墳
衍民之所賴以為生而不能以自遂者也則順
以導之而使之各得其情山林沮澤民之所資
以為用而不能以皆平者也則平以處之而使
punctuated:
第壹場
四書
「因民之所利而利之，斯不亦惠而不費乎？」
王騰鵬

同考試官訓導張，批〔利民之事甚多，數而言之，祇見纒繞。此作獨隱括無遺，至不費處，尤說得精切。得古〕〔人如斯，區區之責塞矣。〕
同考試官教諭王，批〔渾厚之文，得聖人語意。〕
考試官教諭成，批〔說聖人惠民之政，辭不煩而意自足，可取。〕
考試官教授喻，批〔平淡中有隽永之味，可佳。〕

君子與自然之利，斯為自然之惠也。蓋自然之利，即民之所以為利也。於此而與之，其為惠也奚費哉？昔夫子荅子張五美之問，首及於此，謂夫為政莫先於惠民，惠民每難於不費。於此有道焉：思治世以大德，而因五方之產以利民；知生財有大道，而順四時之和以阜物。如丘陵墳衍，民之所賴以為生而不能以自遂者也，則順以導之，而使之各得其情；山林沮澤，民之所資以為用而不能以皆平者也，則平以處之，而使
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books
“By benefiting the people through that which benefits them, is one not generous without expense?”
Wang Tengpeng

Associate Examiner Zhang, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔There are very many ways to benefit the people; to enumerate them merely makes the discussion tangled. This composition alone encompasses them all without omission. Its treatment of being without expense is especially precise and pertinent. In obtaining someone like the men of antiquity in this way [?], I have discharged my humble responsibility.〕
Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: 〔A substantial and well-rounded composition that captures the meaning of the Sage’s words.〕
Examiner Cheng, Instructor, comments: 〔It explains the Sage’s government for benefiting the people. Its language is economical, yet its meaning is complete. It merits acceptance.〕
Examiner Yu, Professor, comments: 〔Beneath its plainness lies a lasting savor. It is commendable.〕

When the gentleman grants benefits that arise naturally, these constitute generosity that arises naturally. For such natural benefits are precisely what the people rely upon for their advantage. If he grants them these, what expense does his generosity entail? When the Master formerly answered Zizhang’s question about the five excellent qualities, he addressed this first. His meaning was that in governing, nothing takes precedence over benefiting the people, yet benefiting them without expense is often difficult. There is a way to accomplish this: contemplate governing the world through great virtue, and draw upon the products of the five regions to benefit the people; understand that there is a great way to produce wealth, and follow the harmonious course of the four seasons to make things abundant. Take hills, highlands, elevated ground, and plains: the people depend upon these for their livelihood, yet cannot fully realize their potential unaided. Accordingly, guide them in conformity with natural conditions, enabling each to obtain what suits its circumstances. Mountains, forests, marshes, and wetlands provide resources for the people’s use, yet the people cannot secure equitable access to them all. Accordingly, arrange their use equitably, and enable …

title: 正德十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
之各得其分夫如是吾見因天分地之制行在
在仰生成之惠利用厚生之政舉人人蒙樂利
之休是非分吾之所有以予之也盖天下之利
自足以供天下之民吾特從而與之耳奚費之
有哉亦非損吾之所藏以益之也盖天下之財
實足以周天下之用吾特從而理之耳何有於
費哉吁君子之惠民也如此其甚博而其爲道
也如此其甚約所謂五美者此其一也子張能
尊而行之則吾夫子之得邦家者可見矣抑嘗
===
因是而有感於聖人之政焉本乎人情出于禮
義不立異以爲高不矯情以干譽此所以其體
公平正大其用溥徧周悉不但足民而亦可以
足國也彼有委道任術自謂可以得民一有不
給則暴征横歛以繼之不知枝榦雖蕃而本實
先撥矣如爲政何吁禮義不修而誠僞之勢殊
固如是夫
故君子尊德性而道問學致廣大而盡精
微極高明而道中庸温故而知新敦厚
punctuated:
之各得其分。夫如是，吾見因天分地之制行，在在仰生成之惠；利用厚生之政舉，人人蒙樂利之休。是非分吾之所有以予之也，盖天下之利自足以供天下之民，吾特從而與之耳，奚費之有哉？亦非損吾之所藏以益之也，盖天下之財實足以周天下之用，吾特從而理之耳，何有於費哉？吁！君子之惠民也，如此其甚博；而其爲道也，如此其甚約。所謂五美者，此其一也。子張能尊而行之，則吾夫子之得邦家者可見矣。抑嘗因是而有感於聖人之政焉：本乎人情，出于禮義，不立異以爲高，不矯情以干譽。此所以其體公平正大，其用溥徧周悉，不但足民，而亦可以足國也。彼有委道任術，自謂可以得民，一有不給，則暴征横歛以繼之，不知枝榦雖蕃，而本實先撥矣。如爲政何？吁！禮義不修，而誠僞之勢殊，固如是夫！

故君子尊德性而道問學，致廣大而盡精微，極高明而道中庸，温故而知新，敦厚
translation_en:
…so that each receives their proper share. If things are done in this way, I see institutions that follow Heaven and apportion the earth put into practice, with people everywhere looking gratefully to the bounty that gives them life and nurtures them; policies that make resources useful and enrich livelihoods are implemented, and everyone enjoys the blessings of happiness and material well-being. This does not mean dividing up what I possess and giving it to them. The benefits of all under Heaven are themselves sufficient to provide for its people; I merely follow what is already there and make it available to them. What expense is involved? Nor does it mean diminishing my own stores to increase theirs. The wealth of all under Heaven is indeed sufficient to meet all its needs; I merely follow what is already there and manage it. How could this entail expense?

Ah! The gentleman’s beneficence toward the people is so extensive, yet the way he achieves it is so simple. This is one of the so-called five excellent qualities. If Zizhang can honor and practice it, we shall be able to see how our Master would act if entrusted with a state or a noble house.

This has also prompted me to reflect upon the sage’s government. It is rooted in human feelings and proceeds from ritual propriety and righteousness. It does not cultivate eccentricity to appear lofty, nor falsify feelings to seek praise. Thus, in its substance it is impartial, equitable, upright, and great; in its application it is far-reaching, comprehensive, and thorough. It can provide sufficiency not only for the people but also for the state. There are those who abandon the Way and rely on contrivances, claiming that they can thereby win the people. As soon as resources fall short, they resort to oppressive taxation and arbitrary exactions to make up the deficit. They do not realize that, though the branches and trunk may flourish, the root has already been uprooted. How can they govern in this way? Ah! When ritual propriety and righteousness are not cultivated, the consequences of sincerity and falsity diverge—indeed, just so!

Thus the gentleman honors his moral nature and pursues inquiry and learning; he reaches the broad and great while fully exploring the fine and subtle; he attains the lofty and luminous while following the Mean; he reviews the old and thereby learns the new; he deepens his generosity…

title: 正德十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
以崇禮
孫䲕
同考試官教諭賈　批〔講存心致知處體認精切而詞亦不苟〕
必嘗留心於中庸之學者
考試官教諭成　批〔脩德凝道之功此篇盡之矣而一結尤〕
有功於學者録之以式多士
考試官教授喻　批〔説理之文正合如此〕
中庸論君子之脩德凝道而必詳乎存心致知
之事也甚矣道不虛行也君子欲脩德以凝道
===
舍是其何以哉此中庸二十七章言人道也其
意若曰聖人之道大矣君子脩德以凝之果何
所從事耶蓋道體極於至大而具之不外乎心
入於至小而知之必由於學故德性之本然者
所當尊也則敬以持之靜以養之使天命之正
以全足以為立本之地事理之當然者所當知
也則學以聚之問以辨之使下學之功以盡足
以為上達之基是固脩德凝道之大端也而猶
未焉彼心體本自廣大也蔽焉則虧矣是必不
punctuated:
以崇禮。
孫䲕。
同考試官教諭賈，批〔講存心致知處，體認精切，而詞亦不苟〕必嘗留心於中庸之學者。
考試官教諭成，批〔脩德凝道之功，此篇盡之矣，而一結尤〕有功於學者，録之以式多士。
考試官教授喻，批〔説理之文，正合如此〕。
中庸論君子之脩德凝道，而必詳乎存心致知之事也。甚矣，道不虛行也！君子欲脩德以凝道，舍是，其何以哉？此中庸二十七章言人道也。其意若曰：聖人之道大矣，君子脩德以凝之，果何所從事耶？蓋道體極於至大，而具之不外乎心；入於至小，而知之必由於學。故德性之本然者，所當尊也，則敬以持之，靜以養之，使天命之正以全，足以為立本之地；事理之當然者，所當知也，則學以聚之，問以辨之，使下學之功以盡，足以為上達之基。是固脩德凝道之大端也，而猶未焉。彼心體本自廣大也，蔽焉則虧矣，是必不
translation_en:
…thereby exalting ritual propriety.

Sun Pu 孫䲕.

Associate Examiner Jia, Instructor, comments: “In its discussion of preserving the mind and extending knowledge, the understanding is precise and penetrating, and the wording is also carefully considered. The author must have devoted attention to the study of the Doctrine of the Mean.”

Examiner Cheng, Instructor, comments: “This essay fully treats the work of cultivating virtue and firmly establishing the Way. Its conclusion is especially beneficial to students. It is recorded here to serve as a model for the many scholars.”

Examiner Yu, Professor, comments: “Writing that expounds principle should be just like this.”

The Doctrine of the Mean discusses the gentleman’s cultivation of virtue and firm establishment of the Way, necessarily dwelling on the work of preserving the mind and extending knowledge. How truly the Way cannot operate of itself! If the gentleman wishes to cultivate virtue so as to firmly establish the Way, how could he do so apart from this? This is the twenty-seventh chapter of the Doctrine of the Mean, which speaks of the human way. Its meaning is as though it said: Vast is the Way of the sage! If the gentleman cultivates virtue to firmly establish it, to what, precisely, should he devote himself? The substance of the Way extends to the utmost immensity, yet its full presence is nowhere outside the mind; it penetrates the utmost minuteness, yet knowledge of it must come through learning. Thus, the original constitution of one’s moral nature is what one must honor: through reverence one preserves it, and through stillness one nourishes it, keeping intact the correctness conferred by Heaven’s mandate and thereby providing a ground on which to establish the root. The principles governing how affairs ought to be are what one must know: through learning one accumulates knowledge of them, and through questioning one distinguishes them, fully accomplishing the work of learning about things below and thereby providing a foundation for reaching understanding above. These are indeed the chief elements in cultivating virtue and firmly establishing the Way, but they do not exhaust the matter. The substance of the mind is inherently broad and great; when obscured, it becomes impaired. Thus one must not…

title: 正德十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
以一毫私意自蔽以廓其廣大之體於其中所
具精微之理則條分縷析不使有毫釐之差焉
心體本自高明也累焉則塞矣是必不以一毫
私欲自累以極乎高明之域於其間自有中庸
之則則周思審處不使有過不及之謬焉得於
融會之餘固有所已知者時複思繹而涵泳之
功深然理義無窮不可自足則鈎深致遠而日
知乎其所未知也由於體驗之後固有所已能
者終日服膺而敦篤之力固然節文至衆不可
===
踈略則隨事精察而日謹乎其所未謹也夫致
廣大也極高明也温故也敦厚也皆存心之屬
也盡精微也道中庸也知新也崇禮也皆致知
之屬也非存心無以致知而存心者又不可以
不致知脩德凝道之君子可不於此而曲盡其
功乎抑考此章尊德性道問學之言盖自子思
發之所以著脩德凝道之功也至朱子始有存
心致知之說所以發明子思之意而示人以入
德之方最為詳盡而雙峯饒氏乃有疑于是說
punctuated:
以一毫私意自蔽，以廓其廣大之體；於其中所具精微之理，則條分縷析，不使有毫釐之差焉。心體本自高明也，累焉則塞矣。是必不以一毫私欲自累，以極乎高明之域；於其間自有中庸之則，則周思審處，不使有過不及之謬焉。得於融會之餘，固有所已知者，時複思繹，而涵泳之功深；然理義無窮，不可自足，則鈎深致遠，而日知乎其所未知也。由於體驗之後，固有所已能者，終日服膺，而敦篤之力固；然節文至衆，不可踈略，則隨事精察，而日謹乎其所未謹也。夫致廣大也，極高明也，温故也，敦厚也，皆存心之屬也；盡精微也，道中庸也，知新也，崇禮也，皆致知之屬也。非存心無以致知，而存心者又不可以不致知。脩德凝道之君子，可不於此而曲盡其功乎？
抑考此章尊德性、道問學之言，盖自子思發之，所以著脩德凝道之功也。至朱子始有存心致知之說，所以發明子思之意，而示人以入德之方，最為詳盡。而雙峯饒氏乃有疑于是說。
translation_en:
…allow even the slightest selfish intention to obscure oneself, so that the mind’s expansive substance may be fully opened out. As for the subtle principles contained within it, one must distinguish and analyze them strand by strand, permitting not the slightest discrepancy. The substance of the mind is inherently lofty and luminous; once encumbered, it becomes obstructed. One must therefore avoid burdening oneself with even the slightest selfish desire, so as to reach the utmost heights of loftiness and luminosity. As for the standards of the Mean naturally present within it, one must consider them comprehensively and act with careful judgment, allowing no error of excess or deficiency. Through integrating one’s understanding, there are certainly things one already knows: by repeatedly reflecting upon and unfolding their meaning, one deepens the work of immersing oneself in them. Yet principles and rightness are inexhaustible, and one must not become complacent. One must therefore probe the depths and reach into the distance, daily coming to know what one has not yet known. After testing things in personal experience, there are certainly things one can already do: by holding fast to them all day, one makes firm the effort of earnest practice. Yet the particular forms and refinements of ritual are exceedingly numerous and cannot be treated carelessly. One must therefore scrutinize each affair precisely, daily exercising care in matters in which one has not yet been careful. Extending breadth and greatness, reaching the utmost loftiness and luminosity, reviewing what is old, and deepening substantial sincerity all belong to preserving the mind. Exhaustively investigating the subtle, following the Mean, knowing what is new, and honoring ritual all belong to extending knowledge. Without preserving the mind, one has no means of extending knowledge; yet those who preserve the mind must also extend their knowledge. Can the gentleman who cultivates virtue and firmly embodies the Way fail to carry his efforts to completion in every particular here?
Moreover, if we examine this chapter’s words about honoring the moral nature and pursuing inquiry and study, they were first articulated by Zisi to make clear the work of cultivating virtue and firmly embodying the Way. Only with Master Zhu did the explanation in terms of preserving the mind and extending knowledge appear. It elucidates Zisi’s meaning and shows people how to enter into virtue with the greatest fullness and precision. Yet Master Rao of Shuangfeng came to harbor doubts about this explanation…

title: 正德十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
定宇陳氏軰又從而和之別為之詞以立義其
亦異乎朱子之見矣
孟子曰許子必種粟而後食乎曰然許子
必織布而後衣乎曰否許子衣褐許子
冠乎曰冠曰奚冠曰冠素曰自織之與
曰否以粟易之曰許子奚為不自織曰
害於耕曰許子以釜甑爨以鐵耕乎曰
然自為之與曰否以粟易之
白金
同考試官教諭王　批〔農末相濟之意須於下節見之〕
此處言之則露盡而無餘蘊矣此作頗得本旨是故錄之
===
考試官教諭成　批〔問答之文辭繁而不複當是〕
作手
考試官教授喻　批〔明白妥帖〕
大賢於時人歷問其師之所事皆有以得其情
焉蓋事不可以兼為宜乎各致其能以相資也
然則許行所謂並耕而食者於此可以見其不
可為矣昔孟子因陳相道許行之說欲以陰壞
punctuated:
定宇陳氏軰又從而和之，別為之詞以立義，其亦異乎朱子之見矣。

Mencius said, “Must Master Xu grow grain himself before he eats?” The reply was, “Yes.” “Must Master Xu weave cloth himself before he dresses?” The reply was, “No. Master Xu wears coarse cloth.” “Does Master Xu wear a cap?” The reply was, “He does.” “What kind of cap?” “A cap of undyed silk.” “Does he weave it himself?” “No. He exchanges grain for it.” “Why does Master Xu not weave it himself?” “It would interfere with his farming.” “Does Master Xu cook with a cauldron and steamer, and farm with iron implements?” The reply was, “Yes.” “Does he make them himself?” “No. He exchanges grain for them.”

title: 正德十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
分别君子野人之法故歷設問以發之意謂食
以養生而粟乃食之具也許子於粟必自種之
而後食乎陳相曰然盖以不耕不可以得禾許
子固種粟而後食也又謂衣以蔽體而布則衣
之常也許子於布必自織之而後衣乎陳相曰
否盖以無褐不可以卒歲許子之所衣者褐也
若乃冠加於首所以稱乎衣也許子冠乎陳相
曰冠是固與人同也然冠製於人或各異其制
也果奚冠乎陳相曰冠素盖從其所尚也又謂
===
許子之冠固有取於素矣其亦自爲之歟曰否
以粟易之誠以冠之所自出者工也易而用之
亦取諸所有耳冠之爲物可以織而成也奚其
不自織歟陳相曰害於耕誠以彼之所專務者
農也兼而爲之恐妨其所事耳又謂備物致用
人所不免許子爨以釜甑而耕以鐵乎陳相曰
然耕之爨之猶夫人也抑以範金合土人所可
能許子身執其勞而後利其用歟陳相曰否粟
以易之猶夫冠也夫由是數者觀之許子服食
punctuated: 分别君子野人之法，故歷設問以發之。意謂食以養生，而粟乃食之具也。許子於粟，必自種之而後食乎？陳相曰：「然。」盖以不耕不可以得禾，許子固種粟而後食也。又謂衣以蔽體，而布則衣之常也。許子於布，必自織之而後衣乎？陳相曰：「否。」盖以無褐不可以卒歲，許子之所衣者褐也。若乃冠加於首，所以稱乎衣也。許子冠乎？陳相曰：「冠。」是固與人同也。然冠製於人，或各異其制也。果奚冠乎？陳相曰：「冠素。」盖從其所尚也。又謂許子之冠，固有取於素矣，其亦自爲之歟？曰：「否，以粟易之。」誠以冠之所自出者工也，易而用之，亦取諸所有耳。冠之爲物，可以織而成也，奚其不自織歟？陳相曰：「害於耕。」誠以彼之所專務者農也，兼而爲之，恐妨其所事耳。又謂備物致用，人所不免。許子爨以釜甑，而耕以鐵乎？陳相曰：「然。」耕之爨之，猶夫人也。抑以範金合土，人所可能，許子身執其勞而後利其用歟？陳相曰：「否，粟以易之，猶夫冠也。」夫由是數者觀之，許子服食
translation_en:
…the rule distinguishing gentlemen from countryfolk; he therefore posed a succession of questions to bring the matter to light. His meaning was this: food sustains life, and grain supplies that food. Must Master Xu grow grain himself before he eats it? Chen Xiang replied, “Yes.” Since one cannot obtain a crop without tilling, Master Xu indeed grows grain before eating it. He further asked: clothing covers the body, and cloth is the usual material for clothing. Must Master Xu weave cloth himself before wearing it? Chen Xiang replied, “No.” Since one cannot get through the year without coarse clothing, what Master Xu wears is coarse cloth.

As for a cap worn on the head, it serves to match one’s clothing. Does Master Xu wear a cap? Chen Xiang replied, “He does.” In this he is certainly the same as other people. Yet caps are made by people, and their designs may differ. What cap, then, does he wear? Chen Xiang replied, “He wears one of plain silk.” This follows his preference. He further asked: Master Xu’s cap is indeed of plain silk, but does he make it himself? The reply was, “No. He exchanges grain for it.” Indeed, caps come from artisans; exchanging for one and using it simply means drawing on what one possesses. A cap is something that can be made by weaving. Why does he not weave it himself? Chen Xiang replied, “It would interfere with his farming.” Indeed, agriculture is his particular occupation; to undertake both would, he fears, hinder his work.

He further asked: obtaining things and putting them to use is unavoidable for anyone. Does Master Xu cook with a cauldron and steamer, and till with iron implements? Chen Xiang replied, “Yes.” In his tilling and cooking, he is like other people. Yet casting metal and shaping clay are things people can do. Does Master Xu undertake that labor himself before benefiting from their use? Chen Xiang replied, “No. He exchanges grain for them, just as with his cap.” Now, judging from these several instances, Master Xu’s clothing and food…

title: 正德十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
器用皆與人同有無相資亦不能少與人異至
於治天下也獨為耕且為之之說何哉大抵國
無君子固不可以為政國無小人亦不可以為
養上下相成勞逸相濟不易之定理也戰國之
時聖王不作處士橫議往往騁為雄辭逸辯以
驚動世主君子小人之法撓於許行之並耕堯
舜中正之道壞於白圭之輕稅而不知其離常
叛道卒不可行也非有孟子精析而明辯之吾
聖賢經世之道將胥而夷矣吁垂世立敎之功
===
豈但闢楊墨而已哉
易
貞固足以幹事
孫轔

考試官教授喻　批〔詞潔理精〕〔眞是易之文字〕
punctuated:
器用皆與人同，有無相資，亦不能少與人異。至於治天下也，獨為耕且為之之說，何哉？大抵國無君子，固不可以為政；國無小人，亦不可以為養。上下相成，勞逸相濟，不易之定理也。戰國之時，聖王不作，處士橫議，往往騁為雄辭逸辯，以驚動世主。君子小人之法，撓於許行之並耕；堯舜中正之道，壞於白圭之輕稅。而不知其離常叛道，卒不可行也。非有孟子精析而明辯之，吾聖賢經世之道，將胥而夷矣。吁！垂世立敎之功，豈但闢楊墨而已哉！

易
貞固足以幹事。
孫轔

translation_en:
…and utensils are all the same as other people’s. In exchanging what he has for what he lacks, too, he cannot differ in the slightest from others. When it comes to governing the realm, however, why does he alone advance the doctrine that one should farm while also governing? Generally speaking, without gentlemen a state cannot be governed; without common people it cannot be provisioned. Those above and below complete one another, and toil and ease complement one another: this is an unchanging principle. During the Warring States period, no sage king arose, and scholars out of office indulged in unrestrained debate, often displaying imposing rhetoric and extravagant arguments to startle the rulers of their age. The proper ordering of gentlemen and common people was disrupted by Xu Xing’s doctrine that all should farm together; the balanced and upright Way of Yao and Shun was undermined by Bai Gui’s low taxation. Yet they did not realize that their doctrines departed from enduring norms and betrayed the Way, and ultimately could not be put into practice. Had Mencius not analyzed these matters precisely and distinguished them clearly, the Way by which our sages and worthies ordered the world would have been swept away altogether. Ah! Was his achievement in establishing teachings for posterity confined merely to refuting Yang Zhu and Mo Di?

Book of Changes
“Correctness and firmness suffice to manage affairs.”
Sun Lin 孫轔

This is exceedingly tedious and tiresome. Among essays that are clear, refined, and pleasing to the mind, this one is the best. It should be recorded as a model.〕

Comment by Examiner Cheng, Instructor: 〔He expounds the meaning of correctness and firmness as though he himself possessed these qualities; he must be someone capable of managing affairs. In placing him among the foremost, we value more than his writing alone.〕

Comments by Examiner Yu, Professor: 〔The language is lucid and concise; the reasoning is precise.〕〔This is truly writing befitting the Book of Changes.〕

title: 正德十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
惟金夫智之德自立夫事之本文言論君子然
也蓋知正之所在而固守之則智之德全矣君
子能然事豈有不立者哉文言申彖傳之意及
此謂夫天道非貞無以成萬物君子非智無以
應萬事其在天之貞於人為智固事之幹矣君
子體之果何如哉是故廣大光明知貞之所在
而持守極其精切知正之所存而操存
極其固本然之正理堅定於心胸他岐不能惑
也當然之正道精專於念慮外物不能移也彼
===
見理不真者易於眩惑而事莫振舉守正不固
者易於撓亂而事恒叢脞惟夫知貞而持守既
堅其所以應酬天下之事中有宰制彼皆依之
以立矣豈不足以幹事乎惟夫知正而操存既
固其所以綜理天下之事中有主統彼皆倚之
以舉矣又不足以幹事乎正理堅定於心胸則
大本已安事無大小由是可行一本立而道生
也正道精專於念慮則大體已定事無常變由
是可處一體立而用行也吁君子以智而幹事
punctuated: 惟金夫智之德，自立夫事之本，《文言》論君子然也。蓋知正之所在而固守之，則智之德全矣。君子能然，事豈有不立者哉？《文言》申《彖傳》之意及此，謂夫天道非貞無以成萬物，君子非智無以應萬事。其在天之貞，於人為智，固事之幹矣。君子體之，果何如哉？是故廣大光明，知貞之所在而持守極其精切；知正之所存而操存極其固。本然之正理堅定於心胸，他岐不能惑也；當然之正道精專於念慮，外物不能移也。彼見理不真者，易於眩惑，而事莫振舉；守正不固者，易於撓亂，而事恒叢脞。惟夫知貞而持守既堅，其所以應酬天下之事，中有宰制，彼皆依之以立矣，豈不足以幹事乎？惟夫知正而操存既固，其所以綜理天下之事，中有主統，彼皆倚之以舉矣，又不足以幹事乎？正理堅定於心胸，則大本已安，事無大小，由是可行，一本立而道生也；正道精專於念慮，則大體已定，事無常變，由是可處，一體立而用行也。吁！君子以智而幹事
translation_en:
Only by [perfecting?] the virtue of wisdom does one establish the foundation of affairs [?]: such is what the Commentary on the Words of the Text (Wenyan) says of the noble man. For when one knows where correctness lies and firmly holds to it, the virtue of wisdom is complete. If the noble man can do this, how could any undertaking fail to be established? The Commentary on the Words of the Text extends the meaning of the Commentary on the Judgments (Tuanzhuan) to this point: without steadfast correctness, the Way of Heaven cannot bring the myriad things to completion; without wisdom, the noble man cannot respond to the myriad affairs. What in Heaven is steadfast correctness is, in human beings, wisdom: it is indeed the mainstay of affairs. What, then, does it mean for the noble man to embody it?

Thus, broad and luminous in understanding, he knows where steadfast correctness lies and holds to it with the utmost precision and care; he knows where what is right resides and preserves it with the utmost firmness. The inherently correct principles are firmly fixed in his heart and mind, so divergent paths cannot mislead him. The correct Way that ought to be followed is the concentrated focus of his thoughts, so external things cannot sway him. Those who do not truly perceive principle are easily bewildered, and their affairs cannot be brought forward; those who do not firmly hold to correctness are easily unsettled, and their affairs are continually confused and disordered. Only when one knows steadfast correctness and holds to it firmly is there an inner authority governing one's responses to the affairs of the world; all those affairs depend upon it for their establishment. Is this not sufficient to serve as the mainstay of affairs? Only when one knows what is right and firmly preserves it is there an inner governing unity in one's management of the affairs of the world; all those affairs rely upon it to be carried out. Is this, too, not sufficient to serve as the mainstay of affairs?

When correct principles are firmly fixed in the heart and mind, the great foundation is secure. Affairs, whether great or small, can thereby be carried out: once the single root is established, the Way comes into being. When the correct Way is the concentrated focus of one's thoughts, the fundamental substance is settled. Affairs, whether routine or exceptional, can thereby be dealt with: once the single substance is established, its functioning proceeds. Ah! The noble man, through wisdom, serves as the mainstay of affairs…

title: 正德十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
是即天道以貞而成物則夫在天者豈不在於
人哉抑論之仁義禮智皆天所予之德君子行
之仁曰體義曰利禮曰嘉用功於一字而已矣
惟智則曰貞固是其用功殆有甚焉者蓋智非
貞固則其流弊或為權謀或為詐術於事非徒
無益而又害之寧不褻天之所予哉世謂踈通
者能幹事貞固者不能幹事其知智之旨否也
物畜然後有禮故受之以履履而泰然後
安故受之以泰
李秉彝
===

人聚而禮始生禮和而心始定此易卦相承之
序也蓋禮因人而起以和為貴也然則小畜履
泰相次之義得非有取於是乎且萬物散殊固
punctuated:
是即天道以貞而成物，則夫在天者豈不在於人哉？抑論之，仁義禮智皆天所予之德，君子行之，仁曰體，義曰利，禮曰嘉，用功於一字而已矣。惟智則曰貞固，是其用功殆有甚焉者。蓋智非貞固，則其流弊或為權謀，或為詐術，於事非徒無益，而又害之，寧不褻天之所予哉？世謂踈通者能幹事，貞固者不能幹事，其知智之旨否也？

物畜然後有禮，故受之以履；履而泰然後安，故受之以泰。

translation_en:
…This is precisely how the Way of Heaven brings things to completion through steadfastness. Is not what resides in Heaven also present in human beings? To discuss this further, benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom are all virtues bestowed by Heaven. In practicing them, the gentleman is told to “embody” benevolence, to “benefit” through righteousness, and to “make excellent” through ritual propriety: in each case, his effort centers on a single word. Only of wisdom is it said that one must be “steadfast and firm”; here the effort required would seem to be greater. For without steadfastness and firmness, wisdom may degenerate into scheming or deceitful techniques. It then not only fails to benefit affairs but actually harms them. Would this not profane what Heaven has bestowed? People say that those who are broad-minded and adaptable can manage affairs, while those who are steadfast and firm cannot. Do they understand the purport of wisdom?

“Only after things have been gathered together is there ritual propriety; therefore, it is followed by Treading (Lü). Only after treading leads to peace is there security; therefore, it is followed by Peace (Tai).”
By Li Bingyi.

This essay alone is vigorous and ample〕〔[?], and its purport [illegible]; its author must possess learning [?] and exertion [?].〕 It certainly deserves to be singled out for advancement.

title: 正德十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
禮之所自生也使渙而不聚則禮隱矣故物之
畜也必親踈少長翕然而畢集尊卑貴賤𦘕然
而萃止然後親踈有殺少長有序而禮制行矣
尊卑有分貴賤有等而名分辨矣拜起坐立之
節每形於相接之頃否則無從施也品秩儀章
之等每著於交會之間否則不可見也是小畜
之與履其義相須自不可易履之次於小畜其
義良有取於此歟至若禮有定分宜人之所必
安也使嚴而不泰則人心離矣故人之行禮也
===
必順其自然無事乎矯飾從容而不迫也行所
無事不假於勉強安舒而自得也然後上下各
安其分而無携貳之心彼此各得其所而無觖
望之念情順意愜從事於畏愛之中怡然而順
適也體習心安不越乎禮制之外帖然而厭服
也是履之與泰其序相因自不容亂泰之所以
次於履其義端有在於是矣吁易卦相承之序
各有一定之理如此信非文王不能定非孔子
無以明也歟大抵禮者人之防其要在敬與和
punctuated: 禮之所自生也。使渙而不聚，則禮隱矣。故物之畜也，必親踈少長翕然而畢集，尊卑貴賤𦘕然而萃止，然後親踈有殺，少長有序，而禮制行矣；尊卑有分，貴賤有等，而名分辨矣。拜起坐立之節，每形於相接之頃，否則無從施也；品秩儀章之等，每著於交會之間，否則不可見也。是小畜之與履，其義相須，自不可易。履之次於小畜，其義良有取於此歟！至若禮有定分，宜人之所必安也。使嚴而不泰，則人心離矣。故人之行禮也，必順其自然，無事乎矯飾，從容而不迫也；行所無事，不假於勉強，安舒而自得也。然後上下各安其分，而無携貳之心；彼此各得其所，而無觖望之念。情順意愜，從事於畏愛之中，怡然而順適也；體習心安，不越乎禮制之外，帖然而厭服也。是履之與泰，其序相因，自不容亂。泰之所以次於履，其義端有在於是矣。吁！易卦相承之序，各有一定之理如此，信非文王不能定，非孔子無以明也歟！大抵禮者，人之防，其要在敬與和
translation_en:
…is that from which ritual arises. If things disperse without gathering, ritual remains hidden. Thus, when things accumulate, close and distant kin, young and old, must all gather together in accord, and those of higher and lower standing, noble and humble, assemble distinctly [?]. Only then are degrees of closeness observed among kin and an order established between young and old, so that ritual institutions operate; distinctions between higher and lower standing and gradations between noble and humble are established, so that titles and stations are clearly differentiated. The prescribed forms of bowing, rising, sitting, and standing manifest themselves whenever people meet; otherwise, there is no occasion to perform them. The gradations of rank and ceremonial insignia become apparent when people gather; otherwise, they cannot be seen. Thus Small Taming (Xiaoxu) and Treading (Lü) require one another in their meanings, and their order cannot be reversed. Surely this is the meaning behind Treading’s following Small Taming!

As for ritual’s fixed distinctions, these should necessarily be positions in which people feel at ease. If ritual is severe without ease, people’s hearts become estranged. Thus, in practicing ritual, people must follow what is natural, without resorting to affectation, remaining composed and unhurried. They must act without contrivance, without relying on forced effort, remaining relaxed and at ease with themselves. Only then do superiors and inferiors each rest content in their stations, without thoughts of disaffection or divided loyalty; each person finds a proper place, without feelings of dissatisfaction or resentment. With feelings harmonious and intentions satisfied, they act within the bounds of reverence and affection, joyfully and willingly accommodating themselves. With their bodies habituated and their hearts at ease, they remain within the bounds of ritual institutions, peacefully and fully submitting. Thus Treading and Peace (Tai) follow one another in a sequence that cannot be disturbed. This, precisely, is why Peace follows Treading.

Ah! Each succession of hexagrams in the Changes has a fixed principle such as this. Surely none but King Wen could have established their order, and none but Confucius could have clarified it! Broadly speaking, ritual serves as a restraint upon people, and its essentials lie in reverence and harmony…

title: 正德十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
而已然樂勝則流固為用和之弊而禮勝則離
亦有過嚴之愆先王制禮體用無全嚴泰相濟
蓋取諸易有子論禮以和為貴而以一于和為
不可行則又本諸先王之意矣後世為禮一以
嚴峻繩下而俾人勉從殆把持之説耳要其流
弊已于先王之制畔已尚可以言易哉
書
安汝止惟幾惟康其弼直惟動丕應徯志
以昭受上帝天其申命用休
李嶽鍾
===
同考試官教諭王　批〔帝王謹位要以内外交脩為重此篇足以發之　蓋善學書者〕
考試官教諭成　批〔講交脩協應之間貫串明白視它作支離排比者大相遠矣〕
考試官教授喻　批〔典則平正〕
大臣推謹位之意必内外之交脩而天人之協
應也甚矣自治在君而輔君則在臣也苟能于
此而交脩焉則夫天人之應蓋有不期然而然
punctuated:
而已。然樂勝則流，固為用和之弊；而禮勝則離，亦有過嚴之愆。先王制禮，體用無全，嚴泰相濟，蓋取諸易。有子論禮，以和為貴，而以一于和為不可行，則又本諸先王之意矣。後世為禮，一以嚴峻繩下，而俾人勉從，殆把持之説耳。要其流弊，已于先王之制畔已，尚可以言易哉？
書
「安汝止，惟幾惟康；其弼直，惟動丕應徯志，以昭受上帝，天其申命用休。」
李嶽鍾
同考試官教諭王，批〔帝王謹位，要以内外交脩為重。此篇足以發之，蓋善學書者。〕
考試官教諭成，批〔講交脩協應之間，貫串明白，視它作支離排比者，大相遠矣。〕
考試官教授喻，批〔典則平正。〕
大臣推謹位之意，必内外之交脩，而天人之協應也。甚矣，自治在君，而輔君則在臣也！苟能于此而交脩焉，則夫天人之應，蓋有不期然而然
translation_en:
…and nothing more. Yet when music predominates, it leads to excess: this is indeed the danger of employing harmony. When ritual predominates, however, it produces estrangement: this too is the fault of excessive severity. When the former kings established ritual, its substance and application were “without completeness” [?]; severity and ease complemented one another. They surely drew this from the Changes. In discussing ritual, Youzi prized harmony but held that exclusive devotion to harmony would not work. He likewise grounded his view in the intentions of the former kings. In later ages, those who instituted ritual subjected their inferiors entirely to severe restraints and compelled reluctant obedience. This amounts to little more than a doctrine of control. Examining its eventual abuses, we find that it has already departed from the institutions of the former kings. Can one still speak of this as understanding the Changes?

Book of Documents

“Rest securely in your proper place; attend to the incipient workings of affairs and to their peaceful outcome. Let those who assist you be upright. Whenever you act, all will respond fully and await your intentions. Thus you will illustriously receive the favor of the Lord on High, and Heaven will renew its mandate with blessings.”

Li Yuezhong

Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: 〔For emperors and kings to exercise due care in their position, they must give priority to mutual cultivation within and without. This essay adequately brings out that point. Its author is surely a good student of the Documents.〕

Examiner Cheng, Instructor, comments: 〔Its discussion of mutual cultivation and harmonious response is coherent and clear. It is far superior to other compositions with their disconnected arrangements of parallel phrases.〕

Examiner Yu, Professor, comments: 〔Classically grounded, well regulated, balanced, and correct.〕

When a great minister expounds the meaning of exercising due care in the sovereign’s position, he must address mutual cultivation within and without, and the harmonious response of Heaven and humanity. How vital this is! Governing himself rests with the ruler, while assisting the ruler rests with his ministers. If they can cultivate themselves mutually in this respect, then the response of Heaven and humanity will surely come about without being sought…

title: 正德十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
者矣昔大禹推所以謹位之意以告于舜其意
謂夫君人固以謹位爲先而謹位尤以交脩爲
要是故人君一心萬化之本也要必順適乎道
心之正不陷于人欲之危俾動靜云爲無不得
所止焉人君一日萬幾之繁也要必將爲而審
其事之所發既爲而省其事之所安俾禮樂刑
政無不得其宜焉則君德之脩于內者密矣然
或一念之未善也輔弼之臣又皆繩君之愆以
格其非心務有以端天下之本其或一事之未
===
臧也左右之職又皆糾君之謬以引于當道期
有以成天下之務則君德之脩于外者至矣如
是則君道允協于民志聖德克享乎天心是惟
無動則已如其動而見于言也匪徒民莫不信
而且歆望于未言之先如其動而見于行也匪
徒民莫不悅而且預待于未行之始徵之于民
民豈我違乎以是昭格于天荷天之休不惟尊
爲天子而已天休滋至大寶之位永固而不搖
也荷天之寵不惟富有四海而已眷命愈加神
punctuated: 者矣。昔大禹推所以謹位之意以告于舜，其意謂夫君人固以謹位爲先，而謹位尤以交脩爲要。是故人君一心，萬化之本也，要必順適乎道心之正，不陷于人欲之危，俾動靜云爲無不得所止焉。人君一日，萬幾之繁也，要必將爲而審其事之所發，既爲而省其事之所安，俾禮樂刑政無不得其宜焉，則君德之脩于內者密矣。然或一念之未善也，輔弼之臣又皆繩君之愆，以格其非心，務有以端天下之本；其或一事之未臧也，左右之職又皆糾君之謬，以引于當道，期有以成天下之務，則君德之脩于外者至矣。如是，則君道允協于民志，聖德克享乎天心。是惟無動則已，如其動而見于言也，匪徒民莫不信，而且歆望于未言之先；如其動而見于行也，匪徒民莫不悅，而且預待于未行之始。徵之于民，民豈我違乎？以是昭格于天，荷天之休，不惟尊爲天子而已，天休滋至，大寶之位永固而不搖也；荷天之寵，不惟富有四海而已，眷命愈加，神
translation_en:
…such a response will indeed arise. Long ago, the Great Yu expounded to Shun the meaning of exercising care in occupying the throne. His meaning was that, although a ruler’s first priority is to exercise care in his position, the essential means of doing so is cultivation both within and without. Thus, the ruler’s mind is the root of all transformations. He must follow the rectitude of the moral mind and avoid falling into the perils of human desires, so that in activity and repose, in speech and action, he always rests where he ought. In a single day, the ruler faces the complexity of myriad affairs. Before acting, he must scrutinize the source from which an undertaking arises; after acting, he must examine where it has come to rest, so that ritual, music, punishments, and government all attain their proper measure. Then the inward cultivation of the ruler’s virtue will be meticulous. Yet if even one thought is not good, the ministers who assist him must all correct his faults and rectify his wayward mind, striving thereby to set right the root of all under Heaven. If even one undertaking is not good, those serving at his side must all correct his errors and guide him onto the proper path, seeking thereby to bring the affairs of all under Heaven to completion. Then the cultivation of the ruler’s virtue from without will be complete.

In this way, the ruler’s way will truly accord with the people’s aspirations, and his sagely virtue will find acceptance in Heaven’s heart. If he makes no move, there is nothing further to say; but when his movement manifests itself in speech, not only will all the people trust him, they will eagerly look forward to his words before he speaks. When his movement manifests itself in action, not only will all the people rejoice, they will anticipate his deeds before he acts. Tested against the people, how could the people oppose me? Through this, he manifestly reaches Heaven and receives Heaven’s blessings. It is not merely that he is honored as the Son of Heaven: Heaven’s blessings arrive in ever greater abundance, and his position upon the precious throne remains forever secure and unshaken. He receives Heaven’s favor. It is not merely that he possesses the wealth of all within the Four Seas: Heaven’s gracious mandate is increasingly bestowed, and the sacred…

title: 正德十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
器之重永建而不拔也儆之于天天豈我違乎
吁人君能盡交脩之道其感應之機如此謹位
之要孰有加于此哉抑大禹陳謨之時水土平
治粒食奏功而舜也惟精惟一庶政維和當時
四方風動曆數在躬其宅心處事格天感民如
禹所謂謹位者舜何待于儆戒而能之耶易曰
危者安其位者也亡者保其存者也古人愛君
類如此彼昏朝末季倡爲豐亨豫大以逢君者
其不爲大禹之罪人哉
===
申畫郊圻慎固封守以康四海
郭大經
同考試官教諭王　批　〔申畫慎固處造語分〕
曉得康王致命本意
考試官教諭成　批　〔畢公一篇爲殷頑民〕
而發此意隱然見之不獨取其詞而已
考試官教授喻　批　〔文字峻整可嘉〕
賈王告大臣欲新畿內之防以安天下之大蓋
王畿天下之本也使非申嚴以爲之防焉其何
punctuated:
器之重，永建而不拔也。儆之于天，天豈我違乎？吁！人君能盡交脩之道，其感應之機如此，謹位之要，孰有加于此哉？抑大禹陳謨之時，水土平治，粒食奏功，而舜也惟精惟一，庶政維和。當時四方風動，曆數在躬，其宅心處事，格天感民，如禹所謂謹位者，舜何待于儆戒而能之耶？《易》曰：「危者，安其位者也；亡者，保其存者也。」古人愛君，類如此。彼昏朝末季，倡爲豐亨豫大以逢君者，其不爲大禹之罪人哉？
申畫郊圻，慎固封守，以康四海。
郭大經
同考試官教諭王批：〔申畫慎固處造語分〕曉，得康王致命本意。
考試官教諭成批：〔畢公一篇爲殷頑民〕而發，此意隱然見之，不獨取其詞而已。
考試官教授喻批：〔文字峻整可嘉〕。
賈王告大臣，欲新畿內之防，以安天下之大。蓋王畿，天下之本也。使非申嚴以爲之防焉，其何
translation_en:
…the weighty vessel of sovereignty will remain established forever, never to be uprooted. Admonishing Heaven [?]—how could Heaven oppose me?
Ah! If a ruler fully pursues the way of cultivating himself both inwardly and outwardly, the workings of stimulus and response are like this. What could surpass this as the essential means of attending carefully to his position? Yet when the Great Yu presented his counsels, the waters and lands had been brought into order, and the work of providing grain for food had succeeded. Shun, maintaining refinement and singleness of purpose, kept every branch of government in harmony. At that time, the four quarters responded as grass bends before the wind, and Heaven’s succession rested in his person. In his intentions and conduct of affairs, he reached Heaven and moved the people. As for what Yu called attending carefully to his position, why would Shun have needed admonition before he could do it? The Book of Changes says: “He who is in danger is one who rests secure in his position; he who perishes is one who safeguards his continued existence.” Such was the way the ancients loved their rulers. Those who, in benighted courts and declining ages, proclaimed abundance, prosperity, ease, and grandeur to gratify their rulers—were they not offenders against the Great Yu?
“Reaffirm the demarcation of the capital’s suburbs and boundaries; carefully strengthen its territorial defenses, thereby bringing peace to all within the Four Seas.”
Guo Dajing
Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: “The phrasing of ‘reaffirm the demarcation’ and ‘carefully strengthen’ is clear and captures King Kang’s original intention in issuing the charge.”
Comment by Examiner Cheng, Instructor: “The entire chapter concerning the Duke of Bi was occasioned by the recalcitrant people of Yin. This meaning is subtly apparent here; the essay does more than merely borrow its wording.”
Comment by Examiner Yu, Professor: “The writing is rigorous and well ordered, and merits praise.”
King Jia [?] addressed his great minister, wishing to renew the defenses within the royal domain so as to bring peace to the vast realm. For the royal domain is the foundation of all under Heaven. Unless its defenses were reaffirmed and made strict, how could he…

title: 正德十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
以安天下也哉昔康王命畢公保釐東郊而告
之至此意謂旌别之典固不可以不舉而根本
之勢尤不可以不嚴是故郊圻之制規畫于開
創之初久矣然歲久則易湮安保其不混淆乎
汝必從而申之遠郊百里近郊五十里截然經
理之有倫邦圻在内五服布外井然界限之不
紊則郊圻再新其在今日猶夫在先世也封域
之險規防于締造之始舊矣然世平則易玩寧
保其不懈怠乎汝必即而謹之閑巡鑿之有警
===
而振揚紀律以肅其出入之防因壺榛之有守
而脩明伍兩以壯其捍衛之威則封守如故其
在繼世猶夫在先王也時緝而屢省之如是則
内無慇民反側之虞國勢定矣而四海之廣視
畿甸以爲安危也會見帖然安枕之不驚近無
商民勤操之患國本固矣而天下之大視國都
以爲重輕也但見晏然安堵之不擾井疆之殊
異兆民之讋服也孰得而震撼之是不可以底
于安乎風聲之覃被萬姓之嚮慕也孰得而危
punctuated: 以安天下也哉？昔康王命畢公保釐東郊，而告之至此，意謂旌别之典固不可以不舉，而根本之勢尤不可以不嚴。是故郊圻之制，規畫于開創之初久矣，然歲久則易湮，安保其不混淆乎？汝必從而申之：遠郊百里，近郊五十里，截然經理之有倫；邦圻在内，五服布外，井然界限之不紊。則郊圻再新，其在今日猶夫在先世也。封域之險，規防于締造之始舊矣，然世平則易玩，寧保其不懈怠乎？汝必即而謹之，閑巡鑿之有警，而振揚紀律，以肅其出入之防；因壺榛之有守，而脩明伍兩，以壯其捍衛之威。則封守如故，其在繼世猶夫在先王也。時緝而屢省之，如是則内無慇民反側之虞，國勢定矣。而四海之廣，視畿甸以爲安危也，會見帖然安枕之不驚；近無商民勤操之患，國本固矣。而天下之大，視國都以爲重輕也，但見晏然安堵之不擾。井疆之殊異，兆民之讋服也，孰得而震撼之？是不可以底于安乎？風聲之覃被，萬姓之嚮慕也，孰得而危
translation_en:
…secure all under Heaven? In former times, King Kang commanded the Duke of Bi to safeguard and administer the eastern outskirts, and his admonition reached this point. His meaning was that the institutions for distinguishing people according to their conduct must certainly be implemented, but that the position of the realm’s foundation must above all be made secure. Thus, the arrangements for the suburbs and royal domain had long since been planned at the dynasty’s founding. Yet with the passage of years they could easily fall into obscurity: how could one guarantee that they would not become confused? You must therefore reaffirm them: the outer suburbs extending one hundred li and the inner suburbs fifty li, distinctly ordered and systematically administered; the royal domain within and the five zones of service arrayed outside, their boundaries clearly delineated and free from confusion. Then the suburbs and royal domain will be renewed, and their condition today will be as it was in earlier generations.

The defenses afforded by the territory’s natural barriers had likewise been planned long ago, at the beginning of the dynasty. Yet in peaceful times they could easily be treated lightly: how could one guarantee that vigilance would not slacken? You must therefore attend to them carefully. Maintain vigilance through patrols and excavated defenses [?], and enforce discipline to make strict the controls on entry and exit; rely upon the guards at the barriers [?], and put the five-man squads and twenty-five-man units in good order to strengthen their defensive power. Then the territorial defenses will remain as before, under succeeding generations just as under the former kings.

Continually repair them and inspect them repeatedly. In this way, there will be no fear within of unrest among the Yin people [?], and the realm’s position will be stable. The vast lands within the Four Seas look to the royal domain as the measure of their own security or peril: one will consequently see everyone resting peacefully, their sleep undisturbed. Nearby, there will be no trouble from agitation among the Shang people [?], and the foundation of the state will be firm. All under Heaven look to the royal capital as the measure of their own strength or weakness: one will see only peaceful dwelling, free from disturbance. With the field boundaries distinctly marked and the multitudes awed into submission, who could shake them? Could this not bring about security? With the influence of royal authority spreading far and the myriad families turning toward it in admiration, who could imperil …

title: 正德十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
疑之豈不可以幾于靖乎向使王畿未嚴而頑
求天下之安其可得哉竊觀是篇亦爲化殷而
作也是時殷民已化訓矣康王猶欲保釐之畢
公繼君陳以成其終其事務治内尤汲汲於王
畿究心焉夫頑民之反覆周非化之之難也奪
其忠憤之爲難也然則周之頑民得非殷之良
民乎要之二代得天下以仁故其效驗與所以
安養之者如此後世取天下者蔑視勝國爲仇
一切草薙而獸獮之謂非人君之自戕也耶噫
===
詩
三之日于耜四之日舉趾同我婦子饁彼
南畝田畯至喜
彭希曾
同考試官訓導張　批〔七月一題爲食之始此篇始〕
〔終發揮再無餘蘊真得周公忠告之心〕
同考試官教諭王　批〔豳風文字作者類多冗蹶求〕
〔其從容明暢無踰于此〕
考試官教諭成　批〔稼穡勤勞意思彷彿目前可喜〕
punctuated:
疑之？豈不可以幾于靖乎？向使王畿未嚴，而頑求天下之安，其可得哉？竊觀是篇，亦爲化殷而作也。是時殷民已化訓矣，康王猶欲保釐之，畢公繼君陳以成其終。其事務治内，尤汲汲於王畿究心焉。夫頑民之反覆，周非化之之難也，奪其忠憤之爲難也。然則周之頑民，得非殷之良民乎？要之，二代得天下以仁，故其效驗與所以安養之者如此。後世取天下者，蔑視勝國爲仇，一切草薙而獸獮之，謂非人君之自戕也耶？噫！

詩
三之日于耜，四之日舉趾。同我婦子，饁彼南畝，田畯至喜。
彭希曾

同考試官訓導張　批〔七月一題，爲食之始，此篇始〕〔終發揮，再無餘蘊，真得周公忠告之心。〕
同考試官教諭王　批〔豳風文字，作者類多冗蹶，求〕〔其從容明暢，無踰于此。〕
考試官教諭成　批〔稼穡勤勞意思，彷彿目前，可喜。〕
translation_en:
…unsettle them? Could this not bring them close to tranquility? Had the royal domain lacked firm order, yet one stubbornly sought [?] peace throughout the realm, could it have been attained? In my humble view, this chapter too was written to transform the people of Yin. At that time, the people of Yin had already been transformed and become obedient to instruction; nevertheless, King Kang still wished to preserve their welfare and maintain order among them. Duke Bi succeeded Jun Chen to bring this undertaking to completion. His task was to secure order within, and he devoted particular urgency and attention to the royal domain. As for the wavering allegiance of the recalcitrant people, Zhou’s difficulty lay not in transforming them, but in overcoming their loyal indignation. Were Zhou’s recalcitrant people, then, not Yin’s good people? In essence, the two dynasties gained the realm through benevolence; hence these were the results they achieved and the means by which they brought peace and sustenance to the people. Those who gained the realm in later ages contemptuously treated the vanquished state as an enemy, mowing its people down like grass and hunting them like beasts without distinction. Could this be called anything other than a ruler’s destruction of himself? Alas!

Book of Odes
“In the third month, we attend to the ploughshares; in the fourth month, we set our feet to work. Together with our wives and children, we bring food to those southern fields; the agricultural overseer arrives and is pleased.”
Peng Xizeng

Associate Examiner Zhang, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔This topic from “Seventh Month” concerns the beginnings of providing food. This essay, from beginning〕〔to end, develops its meaning without leaving anything unexplored. It truly grasps the intent behind the Duke of Zhou’s earnest admonition.〕
Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: 〔Essays on the “Airs of Bin” are generally prolix and stumbling; if one seeks〕〔an unhurried, clear, and fluent treatment, none surpasses this.〕
Examiner Cheng, Instructor, comments: 〔The sense of toil in sowing and reaping seems to appear before one’s very eyes. Most pleasing.〕

title: 正德十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授喩　批〔說田畯　手喜有情一結尤妙〕
農事勤而農官悦豳民爲食之預也盖農者食
之所自出也豳民於是而致勤焉此其所以致
農官之悦歟昔周公以成王未知稼穡之艱難
故陳后稷公劉風化之所由以敎之若曰民資
於食而食本於農穫之雖在於西成而播之則
始於東作時維三陽正月之日也條風巳順而
農事將興豳民則往彼中田之廬取其耜而治
之缺者致其完敝者復其新及時之用於是乎
===
具矣時至四陽二月之日也土脉巳融而農功
可作豳民則以彼既備之耜舉其足而耕之毎
夫治其私八家助其公終歲之勤於是乎始矣
少者既出于田炊爨有不暇矣老者則率其婦
而往餉之載筐及筥有依于畎畝之間内外服
勞而罔或惰也壯者既服于耕饑渴有不免矣
老者則率其子而往饁之其饟伊黍致餽于田
疇之内少長咸事而無敢嬉也夫治田如是之
早用力如是之齊是以田畯之官以勸農爲職
punctuated:
考試官教授喩批〔說田畯，手喜有情，一結尤妙〕。

農事勤而農官悦，豳民爲食之預也。盖農者，食之所自出也。豳民於是而致勤焉，此其所以致農官之悦歟？昔周公以成王未知稼穡之艱難，故陳后稷、公劉風化之所由以敎之。若曰：民資於食，而食本於農。穫之雖在於西成，而播之則始於東作。時維三陽正月之日也，條風巳順，而農事將興。豳民則往彼中田之廬，取其耜而治之，缺者致其完，敝者復其新，及時之用於是乎具矣。時至四陽二月之日也，土脉巳融，而農功可作。豳民則以彼既備之耜，舉其足而耕之。毎夫治其私，八家助其公，終歲之勤於是乎始矣。少者既出于田，炊爨有不暇矣；老者則率其婦而往餉之，載筐及筥，有依于畎畝之間，内外服勞而罔或惰也。壯者既服于耕，饑渴有不免矣；老者則率其子而往饁之，其饟伊黍，致餽于田疇之内，少長咸事而無敢嬉也。夫治田如是之早，用力如是之齊，是以田畯之官以勸農爲職
translation_en:
Examiner Yu, Professor, comments: 〔The discussion of the agricultural overseer conveys his delight with feeling [?]; the conclusion is especially fine.〕

Diligence in farming delights the agricultural officials: this shows how the people of Bin provide for their food beforehand. Farming is the source from which food comes. The people of Bin devote their efforts to it—is this not what brings delight to the agricultural officials? Formerly, because King Cheng did not understand the hardships of sowing and reaping, the Duke of Zhou set forth the origins of the transforming influence of Hou Ji and Gong Liu to instruct him. It was as though he said: The people depend upon food, and food has its foundation in farming. Though the harvest comes with autumn’s completion, sowing begins with spring’s labors.

It is the first month, when the three yang forces prevail. The northeasterly wind has become favorable, and farming is about to begin. The people of Bin go to their huts amid the fields, take out their plowshares, and put them in order. They make damaged ones whole and restore worn ones to new condition. Thus everything is ready for use at the proper time. When the second month arrives, with its four yang forces, the earth has thawed, and agricultural work can proceed. The people of Bin take their now-prepared plowshares and set foot in the fields to plow. Each husbandman tends his private plot, and the eight households together work the communal plot. Thus the toil of the entire year begins.

Once the younger people have gone out to the fields, they have no leisure to cook. The elders therefore lead their womenfolk out to bring them food. Carrying square and round baskets, they attend them among the furrows and field ridges. Those working within and those working outside all exert themselves, and none is idle. Once the able-bodied have undertaken the plowing, hunger and thirst are unavoidable. The elders therefore lead their children out to bring them meals. Their provisions are millet, delivered into the fields. Young and old alike attend to their tasks, and none dares to play idly.

Since they begin tending the fields so early and exert themselves with such concerted effort, the agricultural overseer, whose official duty is to encourage farming…

title: 正德十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
圉將布上之令以授時也舍止于郊而東作之
已動懽忻之意自溢於巡行之時情志之相孚
矣何假於督責之嚴乎圉將省民之耕以率怠
也稅駕于野而室家之具在恍懌之心自形於
色笑之頃慰勞之不遑矣何有於拂逆之容乎
是則民樂於業而自勸官率其職而不煩此先
公之重農足食而風化之所由興也後王可不
知之哉盖嘗合無逸之書而觀之始終開陳拳
拳乎欲知小人之依何邪盖人君知其艱難則
===
儆戒常存而不敢怠荒罔知則驕驕則逸而禍
亂之所由生故周公以此亟訓於君而蒼姬有
道之長有由然矣後世人臣有繪圖以獻者亦
此意也然則詩書之訓豈非萬世君人者之鑒
哉
於論鼓鍾於樂辟廱鼉鼓逢逢矇瞍奏公
魏琦
同考試官訓導張　批　〔民樂文王之樂難以言喻入　〕
〔縮筆此文典則明揚殊不費力佳士也〕
punctuated:
圉將布上之令以授時也，舍止于郊，而東作之已動，懽忻之意自溢於巡行之時，情志之相孚矣，何假於督責之嚴乎？圉將省民之耕以率怠也，稅駕于野，而室家之具在，恍懌之心自形於色笑之頃，慰勞之不遑矣，何有於拂逆之容乎？是則民樂於業而自勸，官率其職而不煩，此先公之重農足食而風化之所由興也。後王可不知之哉？盖嘗合《無逸》之書而觀之，始終開陳，拳拳乎欲知小人之依，何邪？盖人君知其艱難，則儆戒常存而不敢怠荒；罔知則驕，驕則逸，而禍亂之所由生。故周公以此亟訓於君，而蒼姬有道之長，有由然矣。後世人臣有繪圖以獻者，亦此意也。然則《詩》《書》之訓，豈非萬世君人者之鑒哉？
「於論鼓鍾，於樂辟廱。鼉鼓逢逢，矇瞍奏公。」
魏琦
同考試官訓導張批〔民樂文王之樂，難以言喻，入〕〔縮筆。此文典則明揚，殊不費力，佳士也。〕
translation_en:
…When he is about to promulgate the commands from above and announce the proper seasons for agricultural work [?], he stops in the outskirts and finds that spring cultivation has already begun. His delight naturally overflows as he makes his rounds. Their feelings and intentions accord with one another: what need is there for stern supervision and reprimands? When he is about to inspect the people's plowing and spur on the idle [?], he halts his carriage in the fields and finds the households all present.
