又次之。是故士之生于斯世，将以學聖賢也。周子有曰：「士希賢，賢希聖，聖希天。」然則學之道如何？宜必自朱子始。或謂朱子之學似涉于博物，欲始學于明道，以為入道之方。夫天之生人，氣質不齊，善學者當自量其才而為之。明道渾然天成，不犯人力。士生有明道之資則可，不然則姑從事于朱子主敬窮理之功、克己存誠之妙，可以由濂洛之流，遡洙泗之源，升其堂，入其室矣。末學陋聞，極知踰越，妄議前輩，惟執事進而裁之，幸甚。

第三問
李嶽鍾
同考試官教諭王　批〔大學周禮二書，士子為學貴知其要，不但究其補缺而已。此策獨能發之，其亦平日所學知要者歟？得士如此，可與論學矣。〕
考試官教諭成　批〔場中荅目，于大學旨義聊得彷彿，至論周禮則遠甚已。求其互相發明、鑿鑿可看者，秪見〕
translation_en:
…rank next after them. Thus, scholars born into this world should aspire to learn from the sages and worthies. Master Zhou said: “The scholar aspires to be a worthy; the worthy aspires to be a sage; the sage aspires to accord with Heaven.” What, then, is the proper way to learn? One should certainly begin with Master Zhu. Some say that Master Zhu’s learning seems to extend into encyclopedic knowledge, and wish instead to begin with Mingdao, regarding this as the means of entering the Way. Now, when Heaven brings people into being, their temperaments and endowments are unequal. Those skilled in learning should assess their own abilities and proceed accordingly. Mingdao’s attainment was an integral whole, naturally perfected, without the intrusion of human effort. If a scholar is born with Mingdao’s endowment, this approach is possible. Otherwise, he should for the time being devote himself to Master Zhu’s work of maintaining reverence and investigating principle, and to the subtle practice of overcoming the self and preserving sincerity. He may thereby follow the currents of Lian and Luo back to their source in the Zhu and Si rivers, ascending the hall and entering the inner chamber of the sages’ learning. As a junior student of limited knowledge, I am acutely aware that I have overstepped my bounds in presumptuously discussing my predecessors. I would be most grateful if you would take up these remarks and judge them.

Third Question
Li Yuezhong 李嶽鍾

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: 〔In studying the two books, the Great Learning and the Rites of Zhou, what matters for scholars is to grasp their essentials, not merely to investigate how their missing passages might be supplied. This policy essay alone brings this out. Is its author perhaps someone who has grasped the essentials through his customary studies? Having found a scholar like this, one can discuss learning with him.〕

Comment by Examiner Cheng, Instructor: 〔The answers submitted in this examination barely approximate the meaning of the Great Learning; when they discuss the Rites of Zhou, they fall very far short indeed. In seeking an answer that elucidates the two works through each other and offers definite points worth reading, I have seen only…〕

title: 正德十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
此篇録之以式窮經之士
考試官教授喻　批　明體適用之學吾今于子
與其進也
對爲學之道當因書以會其意而不可妄
意以病乎書也夫聖人脩身之道爲治之
法其可見者必徵於書而書有亡焉則聖
人之意殆不可見矣然書非皆亡也因其
不亡者以求其所亡觀其會通以達其意
則凡見於聖人之書者其致一也而何病
===
於亡哉夫大學周禮皆體用之學也而患
生何足以知之請述所聞以對大學孔氏
之遺書然非始於孔氏也自伏羲神農黄
帝堯舜繼天立極皆是道也而孔子則言
之詳耳周禮周公之制作非始於周公也
自雲鳥紀官以及唐虞建官維百夏商官
倍皆此法也而周公制之備耳夫二書之
所由作如此則上自六經下及孔門之問
荅與子思孟子之書凡言學者雖不同而
punctuated:
此篇，録之以式窮經之士。
考試官教授喻　批：明體適用之學，吾今于子與其進也。
對：爲學之道，當因書以會其意，而不可妄意以病乎書也。夫聖人脩身之道、爲治之法，其可見者必徵於書，而書有亡焉，則聖人之意殆不可見矣。然書非皆亡也，因其不亡者以求其所亡，觀其會通以達其意，則凡見於聖人之書者，其致一也，而何病於亡哉？夫《大學》《周禮》皆體用之學也，而患生何足以知之？請述所聞以對。《大學》，孔氏之遺書，然非始於孔氏也。自伏羲、神農、黄帝、堯、舜繼天立極，皆是道也，而孔子則言之詳耳。《周禮》，周公之制作，非始於周公也。自雲鳥紀官，以及唐虞建官維百、夏商官倍，皆此法也，而周公制之備耳。夫二書之所由作如此，則上自六經，下及孔門之問荅與子思、孟子之書，凡言學者，雖不同而
translation_en:
…this essay. I record it as a model for scholars who seek to fathom the Classics.

Comment by Examiner Yu, Instructor: “As for learning that illuminates the underlying substance and applies it in practice, I now commend your progress.”

Response: The way of learning requires us to apprehend the meaning of books through the books themselves; we must not find fault with them on the basis of arbitrary suppositions. The sages’ way of cultivating themselves and their methods of governing, insofar as these can be discerned, must be verified in books. If portions of those books are lost, the sages’ meaning may seem almost impossible to discern. Yet the books have not been lost in their entirety. If we use what survives to seek what is missing, and examine their connections to comprehend their meaning, then everything found in the sages’ books has a single purport. Why, then, be troubled by what is missing?

The Great Learning and the Rites of Zhou both concern learning in its substance and practical application. Yet how could a student such as I [?] be qualified to understand them? Allow me to respond by setting forth what I have heard. The Great Learning is a book handed down from Kongzi, but its teachings did not originate with him. From the time when Fuxi, Shennong, Huangdi, Yao, and Shun succeeded Heaven and established the supreme standard, this was always the Way; Kongzi merely expounded it in detail. The Rites of Zhou sets forth the institutions created by Zhougong, but these did not originate with him. From the naming of offices after clouds and birds, through the establishment of just one hundred offices under Tang and Yu and twice that number under Xia and Shang, this was always the method; Zhougong merely brought its institutions to completeness.

Such being the origins of these two books, from the Six Classics above down to the questions and answers of Kongzi’s school and the writings of Zisi and Mengzi, all discussions of learning, although they differ, nevertheless …

title: 正德十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
會其意則未有不同矣上自唐虞三代損
益之善下及漢唐宋因循之制莫非其遺
凡言治者雖不同而會其意則亦未有不
同矣得其意則不必病其亡而朱子乃補
格致之章何哉盖格物致知爲入學之始
事而不可有差註疏之陋不足言矣而司
馬光爲世大儒乃以格爲扞格之格禦外
物而可以知至道是說行則幾何而不入
於異端非若釋終始者無損大義而可闕
===
也故朱子取程子之意凡十餘條固皆出
於易之學聚問辯中庸之明善孟子之知
性而非臆度之說盖不得已而補之所以
有功於大學也至於周禮冬官一篇固先
王之制而不可缺秦火之厄爲可恨矣河
間獻王購之不獲取考工記以補之則制
度之書非若義理之學可推而補也考工
記固先秦之遺然其所載皆工匠之事耳
而果有富邦國生萬民之意乎故武帝以
punctuated:
會其意，則未有不同矣。上自唐虞三代損益之善，下及漢唐宋因循之制，莫非其遺。凡言治者，雖不同，而會其意，則亦未有不同矣。得其意，則不必病其亡，而朱子乃補格致之章，何哉？盖格物致知爲入學之始事，而不可有差。註疏之陋，不足言矣；而司馬光爲世大儒，乃以格爲扞格之格，禦外物而可以知至道。是說行，則幾何而不入於異端？非若釋終始者，無損大義而可闕也。故朱子取程子之意，凡十餘條，固皆出於《易》之學聚問辯、《中庸》之明善、《孟子》之知性，而非臆度之說。盖不得已而補之，所以有功於《大學》也。
至於《周禮》冬官一篇，固先王之制而不可缺，秦火之厄爲可恨矣。河間獻王購之不獲，取《考工記》以補之，則制度之書，非若義理之學可推而補也。《考工記》固先秦之遺，然其所載皆工匠之事耳，而果有富邦國、生萬民之意乎？故武帝以
translation_en:
…when their meaning is brought together, there is nothing in which they differ. From the beneficial modifications made under Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties down to the institutions inherited and maintained by the Han, Tang, and Song, all are its legacy. All discussions of governance, though they differ, likewise prove consistent when their meaning is brought together. Once that meaning is grasped, there is no need to lament what has been lost. Why, then, did Master Zhu supplement the chapter on investigating things and extending knowledge? Investigating things and extending knowledge are the first undertakings in learning, and no error can be allowed in them. The inadequacies of the commentaries and subcommentaries scarcely merit discussion. Yet Sima Guang, a great Confucian scholar of his age, interpreted ge, “to investigate,” as the ge in hange, “to obstruct,” holding that one could attain knowledge of the ultimate Way by warding off external things. If this doctrine were to prevail, how long would it take to fall into heterodoxy? This is unlike the explanation of “end and beginning,” which may be omitted without impairing the essential meaning. Thus Master Zhu drew upon Master Cheng’s ideas in more than ten passages, all grounded in the Book of Changes’ teaching of accumulating learning and pursuing inquiry and discrimination, the Doctrine of the Mean’s illumination of goodness, and the Mencius’s knowledge of human nature. These were no speculative assertions. He supplied the missing text only because he had no alternative; this is how he rendered a service to the Great Learning.
As for the “Offices of Winter” chapter of the Rites of Zhou, it certainly embodied the institutions of the former kings and could not be dispensed with. Its destruction in the Qin book burning is deeply regrettable. Prince Xian of Hejian offered to purchase it but could not obtain it, and used the Record of Artificers to fill the gap. A book of institutions, however, is unlike the study of moral principles: its missing parts cannot be supplied through inference. The Record of Artificers is indeed a surviving work from before the Qin, but everything it records concerns the affairs of craftsmen. Does it truly convey the purpose of enriching the states and sustaining all the people? Thus Emperor Wu regarded it as …

title: 正德十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
爲黷亂不經而或又以爲漢儒之附會何
休以爲出於戰國之陰謀皆考工記之陋
有以啓之耳是不必補而強補焉所以有
累於周禮也夫格致之章朱子補之善矣
無復可疑也而近世儒者乃欲以知止有
定之二節爲釋經本文而謂其不亡則所
謂知止者既無所承而本末終始豈足以
盡格物之道哉此不通之論也考工記之
篇漢儒補之陋矣然猶不亂也而陳氏俞
===
氏之論乃以五官之屬近似者取補其數
而謂之不亡夫先王之制其事之相攝皆
有深意存焉無所徵而固析之此一偏之
見也是皆未聞聖賢爲學之道帝王爲治
之法而妄意穿鑿甚矣且今之爲學也其
將本於知乎其將不本於知乎若本於知
也則格物之功不可缺而彼知止者安所
從耶今之言治者將盡同於古乎亦因時
而變通乎如其因時也則先王之意有可
punctuated:
爲黷亂不經，而或又以爲漢儒之附會，何休以爲出於戰國之陰謀，皆考工記之陋有以啓之耳。是不必補而強補焉，所以有累於周禮也。夫格致之章，朱子補之善矣，無復可疑也。而近世儒者乃欲以知止有定之二節爲釋經本文，而謂其不亡，則所謂知止者既無所承，而本末終始豈足以盡格物之道哉？此不通之論也。考工記之篇，漢儒補之陋矣，然猶不亂也。而陳氏、俞氏之論，乃以五官之屬近似者取補其數，而謂之不亡。夫先王之制，其事之相攝皆有深意存焉，無所徵而固析之，此一偏之見也。是皆未聞聖賢爲學之道、帝王爲治之法，而妄意穿鑿甚矣。

且今之爲學也，其將本於知乎？其將不本於知乎？若本於知也，則格物之功不可缺，而彼知止者安所從耶？今之言治者，將盡同於古乎？亦因時而變通乎？如其因時也，則先王之意有可
translation_en:
…regarded it as profaning and disordering the canonical tradition. Others have considered it a contrivance of Han scholars, while He Xiu held that it originated in the covert schemes of the Warring States period. These views were all prompted by the shortcomings of the Record of Artificers (Kaogong ji). This was a case of forcibly supplying a supplement where none was needed, thereby compromising the Rites of Zhou (Zhou li). As for the chapter on investigating things and extending knowledge, Master Zhu supplied an excellent supplement; there is no further room for doubt. Yet scholars of recent times would take the two sections concerning knowing where to rest and attaining settled purpose as the original text explaining the Classic, and claim that the chapter was never lost. But then the reference to knowing where to rest has no preceding explanation on which to depend; and how could roots and branches, endings and beginnings suffice to encompass the way of investigating things? This argument does not hold together. The Han scholars’ use of the Record of Artificers as a supplementary chapter was crude, but at least it did not disrupt the text. Yet the arguments of Mr. Chen and Mr. Yu take similar offices subordinate to the five ministries to fill out the requisite number, and claim that nothing was lost. In the institutions of the former kings, the overlapping responsibilities of offices all embodied profound intentions. To insist on separating them without supporting evidence is a one-sided view. All these scholars have failed to understand the sages’ and worthies’ way of learning and the emperors’ and kings’ methods of government; their arbitrary and strained interpretations have gone very far indeed.

Moreover, should learning today be grounded in knowledge, or should it not? If it is grounded in knowledge, then the work of investigating things cannot be dispensed with. From what, then, could that knowing where to rest proceed? Should those who discuss government today follow antiquity in every respect, or adapt their practices to the times? If they adapt to the times, then the intentions of the former kings offer something that can …

title: 正德十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
推而彼曲爲之補者安所用耶執事所謂
得其要則不病於亡者誠確論也而學者
患未得其要耳故朱子著大學嘗曰敬者
聖學始終之要夫敬之說大矣今姑就其
切於格致者言之涵養本原以爲致知之
地研窮物理以盡求知之功而無助無忘
養之以俟其貫通者一以主敬焉則知無
不致而俗學之博聞異端之頓悟者皆可
以破六經四書所論求知之方一貫而無
===
遺矣程子曰有關雎麟趾之意然後可以
行周官之法度夫仁之說大矣今姑就其
切於冬官者言之如何而富邦國如何而
生萬民營建不過其制力役不違其時則
制雖亡而意存而漢儒之謬補元儒之析
經皆可以破設官分職以爲民極者類推
而不背矣故學患不得其要耳學之至則
道自我出法由我立而彼區區於亡與不
亡之說者亦何暇計哉管見如是不識執
punctuated:
推，而彼曲爲之補者安所用耶？執事所謂「得其要則不病於亡」者，誠確論也，而學者患未得其要耳。故朱子著《大學》，嘗曰：「敬者，聖學始終之要。」夫敬之說大矣，今姑就其切於格致者言之：涵養本原，以爲致知之地；研窮物理，以盡求知之功；而無助無忘，養之以俟其貫通者，一以主敬焉。則知無不致，而俗學之博聞、異端之頓悟者，皆可以破；六經、四書所論求知之方，一貫而無遺矣。
程子曰：「有關雎、麟趾之意，然後可以行周官之法度。」夫仁之說大矣，今姑就其切於冬官者言之：如何而富邦國，如何而生萬民，營建不過其制，力役不違其時，則制雖亡而意存，而漢儒之謬補、元儒之析經，皆可以破；設官分職，以爲民極者，類推而不背矣。故學患不得其要耳。學之至，則道自我出，法由我立，而彼區區於亡與不亡之說者，亦何暇計哉？管見如是，不識執
translation_en:
…be extended by inference; what use, then, are those strained attempts to supply what is missing? Your statement that “if one grasps the essentials, one need not be troubled by what has been lost” is indeed sound. The trouble is simply that scholars have not grasped those essentials. Thus Master Zhu, writing on the Great Learning, once said: “Reverent attentiveness is essential to the learning of the sages from beginning to end.” Reverent attentiveness is a vast subject. For now, let us speak only of its immediate bearing on investigating things and extending knowledge. Nurture the fundamental source to provide the ground for extending knowledge; investigate the principles of things exhaustively to fulfill the work of seeking knowledge; neither force its growth nor neglect it, but nurture it while awaiting comprehensive understanding—all with reverent attentiveness as the guiding principle. Then knowledge will be fully extended, and both the mere erudition of conventional learning and the sudden enlightenment of heterodox teachings can be refuted. The methods of seeking knowledge discussed in the Six Classics and the Four Books will be comprehended through a single unifying principle, with nothing omitted.
Master Cheng said: “Only after possessing the spirit of ‘Guanju’ and ‘Linzhi’ can one put into practice the laws and institutions of the Offices of Zhou.” Humaneness is a vast subject. For now, let us speak only of its immediate bearing on the ‘Winter Offices’: how to enrich the states and how to sustain all the people. If construction does not exceed prescribed limits and labor services do not disregard the proper seasons, then, although the institutions have been lost, their intent survives. Both the erroneous supplementation by Han scholars and the division of the classic by Yuan scholars can thus be refuted. The principles of establishing offices and allocating duties to provide a standard for the people can be extended by analogy without departing from their intent. Thus the trouble in learning is simply failure to grasp its essentials. When learning reaches its highest point, the Way issues from me, and institutions are established by me. What leisure would I then have to reckon with those petty arguments about what has or has not been lost? Such is my limited view; I do not know whether you…

title: 正德十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
事以爲何如
第四問
郭鋆
同考試官訓導彭　批〔五策大抵可觀内論相一策全有斷制且于古人名實歷歷條對無遺錄此一篇以例餘〕
作不但取其博聞也
考試官教諭戍　批〔答此問者爲其人物衆多不言詞堆�louvre則體格排比殊爲可厭若是文字疏通磊落殆〕
不可以時文目之
考試官教授喻　批〔三代以下爲輔相者鮮著格心之功宋儒有定論矣此子獨能悉之蓋嘗留心于忠愛者〕
晚閱此篇喜而不寐
===
論相于三代之下可取其隨事之功而難
定其格心之學夫人主治天下必資輔相
以共成正大光明之業而後天下之政始
出于一而其爲輔相者雖每就事建功其
所以正君之務殆不可後矣三代而上堯
舜禹湯文武之爲君皐陶伊傅周召之爲
punctuated:
事以爲何如？

第四問
郭鋆

同考試官訓導彭批〔五策大抵可觀，内論相一策全有斷制，且于古人名實歷歷條對無遺。錄此一篇以例餘〕作，不但取其博聞也。

考試官教諭戍批〔答此問者，爲其人物衆多，不言詞堆�louvre，則體格排比，殊爲可厭。若是文字，疏通磊落，殆〕不可以時文目之。

考試官教授喻批〔三代以下爲輔相者，鮮著格心之功，宋儒有定論矣。此子獨能悉之，蓋嘗留心于忠愛者。〕晚閱此篇，喜而不寐。

論相于三代之下，可取其隨事之功，而難定其格心之學。夫人主治天下，必資輔相，以共成正大光明之業，而後天下之政始出于一。而其爲輔相者，雖每就事建功，其所以正君之務，殆不可後矣。三代而上，堯舜禹湯文武之爲君，皐陶伊傅周召之爲
translation_en:
…what do you, sir, think of this?

Fourth Question
Guo Yun

Comment by Associate Examiner Peng, Assistant Instructor: “The five policy essays are generally worthy of attention. The essay discussing chief ministers displays decisive judgment throughout; moreover, it answers point by point concerning the reputations and actual achievements of men of antiquity, clearly and without omission. We record this essay as representative of his other compositions, choosing it for more than merely its breadth of learning.”

Comment by Examiner Shu 戍 [?], Instructor: “Because this question involves so many figures, those answering it either pile up words [?] or arrange their compositions in repetitive parallel structures, making them decidedly tiresome. Writing such as this, however, is fluent, open, and vigorous; it can hardly be regarded as conventional examination prose.”

Comment by Examiner Yu, Professor: “Among chief ministers after the Three Dynasties, few achieved notable success in rectifying the ruler’s heart: the scholars of the Song reached a settled judgment on this. This candidate alone has grasped it fully; evidently he has devoted thought to loyalty and loving concern for his ruler. Reading this essay late at night, I was so delighted that I could not sleep.”

In discussing chief ministers after the Three Dynasties, one may commend their achievements in dealing with particular affairs, but it is difficult to establish their learning in rectifying the ruler’s heart. When a sovereign governs the realm, he must rely on chief ministers to accomplish together an undertaking that is upright and enlightened; only then can the government of the realm proceed from a single source. Although those serving as chief ministers continually achieve merit in particular affairs, their task of correcting the ruler must surely not be put last. In the time of the Three Dynasties and earlier, Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu served as rulers, while Gao Yao, Yi Yin, Fu Yue, the Duke of Zhou, and the Duke of Shao served as …

title: 正德十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
臣明良相逢上下一體不可見已秦不師
古亦不足道漢髙帝起自豐沛征伐四方
蕭何守關中營緝根本首薦韓信卒定三
秦天下既定何秉國鈞盡革秦法定一代
規模天下作畫一之歌張南軒稱之宜矣
曹參雖不逮何然以摧鋒陷陣勇敢果銳
之氣施之治民乃能盡斂芒角遵何約法
其人亦寛裕有識矣故張子並及之魏相
之遇宣帝四方有異聞或逆賊災變輙奏
===
言之及諫伐匈奴一書憂勤獨至而南軒
亦嘗取之至若丙吉為相當時政治之不
得刑罰之失中賢否之未辨吉何釋此不
慮乃問牛喘以求隂陽不及魏相遠矣但
其深厚不伐寛緩從事以宣帝之政尚猛
而有矯之之意抑亦太甚乎司馬公非之
盖可知已唐太宗任房玄齡為相本以文
學明達吏事與杜如晦引援士類常如不
及至臺閣規模多所著定夙夜盡心用法
punctuated: 臣，明良相逢，上下一體，不可見已。秦不師古，亦不足道。漢髙帝起自豐沛，征伐四方，蕭何守關中，營緝根本，首薦韓信，卒定三秦。天下既定，何秉國鈞，盡革秦法，定一代規模，天下作畫一之歌，張南軒稱之宜矣。曹參雖不逮何，然以摧鋒陷陣、勇敢果銳之氣施之治民，乃能盡斂芒角，遵何約法，其人亦寛裕有識矣，故張子並及之。魏相之遇宣帝，四方有異聞，或逆賊災變，輙奏言之。及諫伐匈奴一書，憂勤獨至，而南軒亦嘗取之。至若丙吉為相，當時政治之不得、刑罰之失中、賢否之未辨，吉何釋此不慮，乃問牛喘，以求隂陽？不及魏相遠矣。但其深厚不伐，寛緩從事，以宣帝之政尚猛，而有矯之之意，抑亦太甚乎？司馬公非之，盖可知已。唐太宗任房玄齡為相，本以文學明達吏事，與杜如晦引援士類，常如不及。至臺閣規模，多所著定，夙夜盡心，用法
translation_en:
…as ministers: enlightened rulers and worthy ministers met, and those above and below formed a single body—a sight no longer to be seen. Qin did not take antiquity as its model and is likewise not worth discussing. Emperor Gao of Han rose from Feng and Pei and campaigned in all directions. Xiao He held Guanzhong and consolidated the foundations of his rule. He was the first to recommend Han Xin, and the Three Qin were ultimately subdued. Once the realm was settled, Xiao He took the helm of government, completely reformed Qin’s laws, and established the institutions of the dynasty. Throughout the realm people sang of his uniform regulations. Zhang Nanxuan was right to praise him.

Although Cao Can did not equal Xiao He, when he brought to governing the people the spirit of courage, resolution, and daring with which he had broken enemy formations and stormed their lines, he was able to restrain all his sharp edges and follow Xiao He’s simplified laws. He too was generous in disposition and possessed discernment. Thus Master Zhang discussed him alongside Xiao He.

When Wei Xiang enjoyed Emperor Xuan’s favor, whenever unusual reports arrived from any quarter, whether concerning rebels or calamitous portents, he invariably reported them to the throne. His written remonstrance against attacking the Xiongnu displayed exceptional solicitude and diligence, and Nanxuan also commended him for it. As for Bing Ji’s service as Chief Councilor, there were failures of government, punishments that missed the proper measure, and worthy and unworthy men who had not been distinguished. Why did Bing Ji set these aside without concern, instead asking about a panting ox to investigate the workings of yin and yang? He fell far short of Wei Xiang. Yet he was profoundly generous and unassuming, and handled affairs with leniency. Since Emperor Xuan’s government favored severity, he intended to correct it—but was this not also going too far? The reason for Lord Sima’s criticism of him can thus be understood.

Emperor Taizong of Tang appointed Fang Xuanling Chief Councilor, principally because of his literary learning and clear understanding of administrative affairs. Together with Du Ruhui, he recommended and advanced men of ability, always feeling that he had not done enough. He established many of the institutional arrangements of the central government, devoted himself wholeheartedly day and night, and in applying the law…

title: 正德十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
寛平可謂謀斷相資者也然帝定禍亂而
不言功王魏善諫而讓其直英衛善兵而
濟以文是豈區區尺寸者哉迨玄宗始相
姚崇崇即陳十事首舉政先仁恕幷時務
激切以堅帝意帝皆納之其與宋璟雖志
操不同然協心輔帝使賦役寛平刑罰清
慎百姓富庶不求邊功不賞邊臣唐世賢
相前稱房杜後稱姚宋他人莫比焉有宋
韓琦初相仁宗首請建儲大策既相英宗
===
請太后歸政調和兩宮貶斥中侍真安國
家定社稷之名臣方仁宗之相范仲淹也
仲淹皇恐退上十事類皆切于兵民帝欲
以治平責成輔相命仲淹主西事富弼主
北事弼陳時務諸條安邊諸策大畧以進
退賢否裁抑僥倖為先及弼復相神宗極
論變異非數論小人變法所謂學本忠孝
先憂後樂有之歐陽脩之在仁宗其調和
定策之功可比魏公然以文章自任故其
punctuated:
寛平，可謂謀斷相資者也。然帝定禍亂而不言功，王魏善諫而讓其直，英衛善兵而濟以文，是豈區區尺寸者哉！迨玄宗始相姚崇，崇即陳十事，首舉政先仁恕，幷時務激切，以堅帝意，帝皆納之。其與宋璟雖志操不同，然協心輔帝，使賦役寛平，刑罰清慎，百姓富庶，不求邊功，不賞邊臣。唐世賢相，前稱房杜，後稱姚宋，他人莫比焉。
有宋韓琦初相仁宗，首請建儲大策。既相英宗，請太后歸政，調和兩宮，貶斥中侍，真安國家、定社稷之名臣。方仁宗之相范仲淹也，仲淹皇恐，退上十事，類皆切于兵民。帝欲以治平責成輔相，命仲淹主西事，富弼主北事。弼陳時務諸條、安邊諸策，大畧以進退賢否、裁抑僥倖為先。及弼復相神宗，極論變異非數，論小人變法。所謂學本忠孝、先憂後樂，有之。歐陽脩之在仁宗，其調和定策之功可比魏公，然以文章自任，故其
translation_en:
…lenient and equitable: one may indeed say that planning and decision complemented one another. Yet when the emperor quelled disorder, he claimed no credit; when Wang Gui and Wei Zheng excelled in remonstrance, he yielded to their forthrightness; and when the dukes of Ying and Wei excelled in warfare, he complemented their abilities with civil accomplishments. Could these have been merely petty attainments?
When Xuanzong first appointed Yao Chong chief councilor, Chong immediately presented ten proposals. Foremost was that government should give priority to benevolence and forbearance. He also spoke urgently and forcefully about current affairs to strengthen the emperor’s resolve, and the emperor accepted all his proposals. Although Chong and Song Jing differed in their aspirations and principles, they worked together wholeheartedly to assist the emperor. They made taxation and labor service moderate and equitable, administered punishments with integrity and care, and brought prosperity to the people. They neither sought military achievements on the frontier nor rewarded frontier officials. Among the worthy chief councilors of the Tang, Fang Xuanling and Du Ruhui were celebrated in the earlier period, and Yao Chong and Song Jing in the later; no others could compare with them.
Under the Song, when Han Qi first served as chief councilor to Renzong, his foremost request concerned the great policy of establishing an heir apparent. After becoming chief councilor to Yingzong, he asked the empress dowager to return the reins of government, reconciled the two palaces, and demoted and dismissed palace attendants. He was truly an eminent minister who secured the state and stabilized its altars of soil and grain.
When Renzong appointed Fan Zhongyan chief councilor, Zhongyan, deeply apprehensive, withdrew and submitted ten proposals, nearly all directly relevant to the army and the people. Wishing to hold his chief councilors responsible for achieving peace and good government, the emperor ordered Zhongyan to oversee western affairs and Fu Bi to oversee northern affairs. Bi presented proposals on current affairs and plans for securing the frontiers, generally giving priority to advancing the worthy and dismissing the unworthy, and curbing those who sought undeserved favors. When Bi again became chief councilor under Shenzong, he argued emphatically that anomalous phenomena were not simply matters of fate [?], and criticized petty men for changing the established laws. The description of one whose learning was rooted in loyalty and filial devotion, who worried before others and enjoyed happiness after them, applied to him.
During Renzong’s reign, Ouyang Xiu’s achievements in fostering concord and settling the succession could compare with those of the Duke of Wei, Han Qi. Yet he regarded literary composition as his own responsibility, and therefore his…

title: 正德十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
建立不逮三子當時之稱其有意乎蘇子
嘗曰歐陽子今之韓愈也蓋述其道術之
正歷唐至宋僅接于歐子蓋一節之論也
夫鋪觀蕭曹佐高祖之業丙魏輔宣帝之
治其才行器識并其功業之所過前言固
已明白若房杜相太宗致貞觀之隆姚宋
相明皇成開元之治其詳亦自見矣若韓
范富歐之在宋共成慶曆嘉祐之美其器
識如彼才行如彼而其功業如彼是豈爲
===
不遇耶然一暴十寒方任即罷使豪傑之
士不盡所長則亦豈爲全遇哉究其極至
大抵隨時以就功名于古人所謂格正君
心之功率有未盡故其治效終不古若也
何參惟其不學以高帝之資不能贊助遠
追三代之法一時所定如井田封建多襲
秦故參當呂氏之禍著萌不能引義以強
君心逆爲之處以折其謀則又何望于格
君乎丙魏之于漢宣猶蕭曹之于漢高也
punctuated:
建立不逮三子，當時之稱，其有意乎？蘇子嘗曰：「歐陽子，今之韓愈也。」蓋述其道術之正，歷唐至宋，僅接于歐子，蓋一節之論也。
夫鋪觀蕭曹佐高祖之業，丙魏輔宣帝之治，其才行器識，并其功業之所過，前言固已明白。若房杜相太宗，致貞觀之隆；姚宋相明皇，成開元之治，其詳亦自見矣。若韓范富歐之在宋，共成慶曆嘉祐之美，其器識如彼，才行如彼，而其功業如彼，是豈爲不遇耶？然一暴十寒，方任即罷，使豪傑之士不盡所長，則亦豈爲全遇哉？究其極至，大抵隨時以就功名，于古人所謂格正君心之功，率有未盡，故其治效終不古若也。
何參惟其不學，以高帝之資，不能贊助遠追三代之法。一時所定，如井田封建，多襲秦故。參當呂氏之禍著萌，不能引義以強君心，逆爲之處以折其謀，則又何望于格君乎？丙魏之于漢宣，猶蕭曹之于漢高也。
translation_en:
…his achievements fell short of those of the other three masters. Did the praise accorded him at the time have some particular meaning? Master Su once said, “Master Ouyang is the Han Yu of our day.” This presumably referred to the orthodoxy of his Way and learning: from the Tang down to the Song, that tradition was taken up again only by Master Ouyang. It was thus a judgment concerning just one aspect of him.
Consider broadly Xiao He and Cao Shen’s service in establishing Gaozu’s enterprise, and Bing Ji and Wei Xiang’s assistance in Emperor Xuan’s government. Their abilities, conduct, capacity, and discernment, together with the ways in which their achievements surpassed others, have already been made clear above. Likewise, Fang Xuanling and Du Ruhui served as chief ministers to Taizong and brought about the flourishing of the Zhenguan era; Yao Chong and Song Jing served as chief ministers to Minghuang and accomplished the good government of the Kaiyuan era. The particulars are also evident. As for Han Qi, Fan Zhongyan, Fu Bi, and Ouyang Xiu in the Song, they jointly brought about the excellence of the Qingli and Jiayou eras. With such capacity and discernment, such abilities and conduct, and such achievements, how could they be said to have lacked the opportunity to serve? Yet one day of warmth was followed by ten days of cold: scarcely appointed, they were dismissed, preventing outstanding men from fully exercising their strengths. How, then, could they be said to have enjoyed full opportunity? Examining the utmost extent of their accomplishments, we find that they generally adapted to their times to achieve merit and renown. In what the ancients called the work of rectifying the ruler’s mind, they mostly fell short. Thus the results of their government ultimately failed to equal those of antiquity.
Precisely because Xiao He and Cao Shen lacked learning, even with Emperor Gao’s natural gifts they could not assist him in reaching back to emulate the institutions of the Three Dynasties. The arrangements established at the time, in such matters as the well-field system and the enfeoffment of lords, largely followed Qin precedents. When the seeds of the calamity brought about by the Lü clan began to appear, Cao Shen could not invoke righteousness to strengthen the ruler’s resolve, or make advance provision to thwart their designs. What hope, then, was there of his rectifying the ruler? Bing Ji and Wei Xiang’s relationship to Emperor Xuan of Han was like that of Xiao He and Cao Shen to Emperor Gao of Han.

title: 正德十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
以房杜之學而值好名之君姚宋之識而
逢中材之主不復過責已若韓范富歐諸
公所學皆出于正一時建立大有可觀而
惜不以正君為先務豈非天未欲平治天
下哉愚竊論之漢相之不學豈特為格君
之累乎蕭何出私財以助軍費買田宅以
自污以此媚上僅免忌刻終取械繫若魏
相借托許史進不以正則牽制徇從之必
多矣皆未免為才行之累也若韓琦歐陽
===
脩定議濮王典禮互相失之自取范呂之
議胡新安嘗曰歐陽脩倡議以誤韓琦韓
琦主議以誤天下始于講學不明終于執
以私意是又不免為二公所學之累也其
于平生大節亦不相掩吾獨有望于正君
之功非宋之四公不能也而何不為哉孟
子曰人不足與適也政不足與間也惟大
人為能格君心之非君仁莫不仁君義莫
不義一正君而國定矣愚以大臣以道事
punctuated: 以房杜之學，而值好名之君；姚宋之識，而逢中材之主，不復過責已。若韓范富歐諸公，所學皆出于正，一時建立，大有可觀，而惜不以正君為先務，豈非天未欲平治天下哉？愚竊論之，漢相之不學，豈特為格君之累乎？蕭何出私財以助軍費，買田宅以自污，以此媚上，僅免忌刻，終取械繫。若魏相借托許史，進不以正，則牽制徇從之必多矣，皆未免為才行之累也。若韓琦歐陽脩定議濮王典禮，互相失之，自取范呂之議。胡新安嘗曰：「歐陽脩倡議以誤韓琦，韓琦主議以誤天下，始于講學不明，終于執以私意。」是又不免為二公所學之累也。其于平生大節，亦不相掩。吾獨有望于正君之功，非宋之四公不能也，而何不為哉？孟子曰：「人不足與適也，政不足與間也，惟大人為能格君心之非。君仁，莫不仁；君義，莫不義。一正君而國定矣。」愚以大臣以道事
translation_en:
…With the learning of Fang and Du, they nevertheless encountered a ruler who loved renown; with the discernment of Yao and Song, they encountered a ruler of middling ability. We need not demand more of them. As for Han, Fan, Fu, and Ou, their learning all derived from what was correct, and their accomplishments in their day were considerable. Yet regrettably they did not make rectifying their ruler their foremost duty. Was Heaven not yet willing to bring peace and order to the world?

In my humble judgment, did the Han chief ministers’ lack of learning impede only their ability to rectify their rulers? Xiao He contributed his private wealth toward military expenses and purchased fields and houses to sully his own reputation. By thus ingratiating himself with his sovereign, he barely escaped jealous severity and ultimately brought imprisonment in fetters upon himself. As for Wei Xiang, he relied on the Xu and Shi families for support. Since his advancement did not follow the proper path, he must often have been constrained by others and obliged to comply with them. These failings inevitably compromised their abilities and conduct alike.

When Han Qi and Ouyang Xiu settled their position on the ritual honors for the Prince of Pu, they led one another into error and brought upon themselves the criticism of Fan and Lü. Hu Xin’an once said: “Ouyang Xiu initiated the proposal and thereby misled Han Qi; Han Qi championed it and thereby misled the realm. It began with a lack of clarity in their study and ended with their stubborn adherence to personal views.” This, too, inevitably reflected adversely upon the learning of these two men. Yet these faults did not obscure the great integrity they displayed throughout their lives. My particular hope rests upon the achievement of rectifying the ruler: none but these four gentlemen of the Song could have accomplished it. Why, then, did they not do so?

Mencius said: “There is no point in finding fault with individual men, nor in criticizing particular measures of government. Only a great man can rectify what is wrong in the ruler’s heart. When the ruler is benevolent, none are unbenevolent; when the ruler is righteous, none are unrighteous. Once the ruler is rectified, the state is settled.” I believe that a great minister, in serving according to the Way…

title: 正德十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
君未必棋從自當先盡其在我者故曰責
難于君謂之恭陳善閉邪謂之敬吾君不
能謂之賊豈可先謂人主不能而曲所學
以狥之哉嗚呼天下後世為人臣者可以
鑒矣
第五問
賈世祥
同考試官訓導呂　批〔考古之迹固驗其識策時之務以試其才若此作者首尾敘說懇切而廢置傳當信非有用之〕
===
學不能及之高薦固宜
考試官教諭成　批〔言利與理財誠異天理人欲判此一舉終篇先會此義故其一時條荅秩然可行可謂以義〕
為利不以利為利者
考試官教授喻　批〔官民匱竭今日之慮莫先于此子窮居下筆輒能言之周悉詳盡其平日先天下之憂者乎〕
用有常經者足國之道也歛有常制者足
民之道也夫天下之財自有定數歛之則
聚於上散之則藏於民經制有常則公私
punctuated:
君，未必棋從，自當先盡其在我者。故曰：「責難于君謂之恭，陳善閉邪謂之敬，吾君不能謂之賊。」豈可先謂人主不能，而曲所學以狥之哉？嗚呼！天下後世為人臣者，可以鑒矣。
第五問
賈世祥
同考試官訓導呂，批〔考古之迹，固驗其識；策時之務，以試其才。若此作者，首尾敘說懇切，而廢置傳當，信非有用之〕學不能及之，高薦固宜。
考試官教諭成，批〔言利與理財誠異，天理人欲判此一舉。終篇先會此義，故其一時條荅，秩然可行，可謂以義〕為利，不以利為利者。
考試官教授喻，批〔官民匱竭，今日之慮莫先于此。子窮居，下筆輒能言之周悉詳盡，其平日先天下之憂者乎？〕
用有常經者，足國之道也；歛有常制者，足民之道也。夫天下之財，自有定數，歛之則聚於上，散之則藏於民。經制有常，則公私
translation_en:
…the ruler, who may not necessarily comply [?]; one should first fully discharge what lies within one’s own power. Thus it is said: “To demand difficult things of the ruler is called respect; to present what is good and bar what is wrong is called reverence; to say that our ruler is incapable is called betraying him.” How could one pronounce the sovereign incapable beforehand and bend one’s learning to cater to him? Alas! Those who serve as ministers throughout the world and in later generations may take warning from this.
Fifth Question
Jia Shixiang
Associate Examiner Lü, Assistant Instructor, comments: “Examining the traces of antiquity certainly tests a candidate’s discernment; questioning him on the affairs of the present tests his ability. This author’s exposition is earnest from beginning to end, and his proposals for abolishing and establishing measures are appropriate [?]. Such an achievement surely requires learning of practical use. A high recommendation is certainly fitting.”
Examiner Cheng, Instructor, comments: “Speaking of profit and managing finances are indeed different: the distinction between Heaven’s principle and human desire turns on this single matter. Throughout the essay, the author first grasps this meaning; consequently, his itemized responses to current circumstances are orderly and practicable. He may be said to regard righteousness as profit, rather than profit as profit.”
Examiner Yu, Professor, comments: “The exhaustion of official and popular resources—no concern today takes precedence over this. Living in straitened circumstances, you nevertheless take up your brush and discuss it comprehensively and in full detail. Are you one who habitually worries before all others under Heaven?”
To keep expenditure subject to regular principles is the way to provide sufficiently for the state; to keep levies subject to fixed regulations is the way to provide sufficiently for the people. The wealth of the realm has a fixed amount: when collected, it accumulates above; when dispersed, it is stored among the people. If principles and regulations remain constant, then both public and private…

title: 正德十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
之皆足然有至於交困者則費之妄而歛
之横也費之妄則耗於無益歸於私門國
用鈌而歛不得以不横歛之横則民益貧
國益急而禍亂之所由作矣今方承平之
時而以乏財為憂愚生有以諒執事不得
已之心而亦有不容已之對也且生財之
道亦多端矣縱不可以言利而豈無務本
阜貨之類乎而愚固曰用有常經歛有常
制者不近於迂且狹哉顧以今之急病在
===
於妄費横徵而非生財之道鈌焉耳周官
以九賦歛財賄以九式均節財用曰九賦
則賦外無徵也曰九式則式外無費也古
之足國足民之道亦如是而已矣山右土
瘠民貧非東南財賦之比然堯舜禹相繼
都之茅茨土堦非衣惡食如是之儉也晉
之世霸德雖不類而勤儉未衰及築虒祁
之宮富趙魏之室而遂以僨矣此古之明
驗也今地利所出不減於昔時而賦額之
punctuated:
之皆足。然有至於交困者，則費之妄而歛之横也。費之妄，則耗於無益，歸於私門，國用鈌而歛不得以不横；歛之横，則民益貧，國益急，而禍亂之所由作矣。今方承平之時，而以乏財為憂，愚生有以諒執事不得已之心，而亦有不容已之對也。且生財之道亦多端矣，縱不可以言利，而豈無務本阜貨之類乎？而愚固曰用有常經、歛有常制者，不近於迂且狹哉？顧以今之急病在於妄費横徵，而非生財之道鈌焉耳。《周官》以九賦歛財賄，以九式均節財用。曰九賦，則賦外無徵也；曰九式，則式外無費也。古之足國足民之道，亦如是而已矣。

山右土瘠民貧，非東南財賦之比。然堯舜禹相繼都之，茅茨土堦，非衣惡食，如是之儉也。晉之世霸，德雖不類，而勤儉未衰；及築虒祁之宮，富趙魏之室，而遂以僨矣。此古之明驗也。今地利所出不減於昔時，而賦額之
translation_en:
…both have enough. Yet when the state and the people alike fall into distress, it is because expenditure is reckless and exactions are arbitrary. Reckless expenditure wastes resources on useless things and channels them into private households; state funds run short, and exactions inevitably become arbitrary. Arbitrary exactions further impoverish the people and make the state's needs still more pressing: this is how calamity and disorder arise. Now, in a time of peace, a shortage of funds has become a cause for concern. This humble student can therefore appreciate the constraints under which you, gentlemen, act, yet I also have a reply that I cannot withhold. There are, moreover, many ways to generate wealth. Even if one must not speak of profit, are there not such means as attending to agriculture, the fundamental occupation, and increasing the supply of goods? Does my insistence that expenditure follow regular norms and revenue collection follow fixed rules not seem rather impractical and narrow? Yet the urgent malady today lies in reckless expenditure and arbitrary exactions, not in a lack of ways to generate wealth. The Offices of Zhou prescribes collecting wealth through the nine levies and regulating expenditure equitably through the nine standards. “Nine levies” means that no exactions are imposed beyond these levies; “nine standards” means that no expenditure is incurred beyond these standards. The ancients' way of providing enough for both state and people amounted to just this.

Shanyou has poor soil and impoverished people; its tax revenues cannot compare with those of the southeast. Yet Yao, Shun, and Yu successively established their capitals there. Thatched roofs and earthen steps, coarse clothing [?] and poor food—such was their frugality. When Jin held the hegemony, its virtue did not match theirs, but diligence and frugality had not yet declined. Once it built the palace at Siqi and enriched the houses of Zhao and Wei, however, it consequently fell. This is clear evidence from antiquity. Today the land produces no less than it did in former times, while the assessed tax quota…

title: 正德十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
供有寬於別省且濟以鹽之利焉而顧公
私之困乏者愚生固亦有所疑也以為生
齒之繁則自古未聞以民多為患者也以
為天災之流則堯湯之水旱猶不病也其
曰勤儉衰而惰靡衆盖其有焉然勤儉可
率而惰靡可戒也侵漁逋負之弊積盖亦
有焉然侵漁可詰而逋負可追也愚生雖
不達經國之計而頗悉閭閻之隱矣無名
之徵一下郡邑追呼督促雞犬不寧累下
===
則幾倍於常賦急徵則有甚於催科富者
以貧貧者以竭故一遇水旱非流則死耳
然又未聞以供邊儲也未聞以給禄食也
况民財有限橫徵既多則常賦反累而國
用安得以不缺哉故一有警急則束手無
策耳是以公私俱困愚以為橫徵妄費之
致也執事欲急於足國而曰有無變通不
加賦而用足此劉晏制鹽之法也而今之
鹽利已無遺矣况行之未善則其害有甚
punctuated: 供有寬於別省，且濟以鹽之利焉，而顧公私之困乏者，愚生固亦有所疑也。以為生齒之繁，則自古未聞以民多為患者也；以為天災之流，則堯湯之水旱猶不病也。其曰勤儉衰而惰靡衆，盖其有焉，然勤儉可率而惰靡可戒也。侵漁逋負之弊積，盖亦有焉，然侵漁可詰而逋負可追也。愚生雖不達經國之計，而頗悉閭閻之隱矣。無名之徵一下郡邑，追呼督促，雞犬不寧；累下則幾倍於常賦，急徵則有甚於催科。富者以貧，貧者以竭，故一遇水旱，非流則死耳。然又未聞以供邊儲也，未聞以給禄食也。况民財有限，橫徵既多，則常賦反累，而國用安得以不缺哉？故一有警急，則束手無策耳。是以公私俱困，愚以為橫徵妄費之致也。執事欲急於足國，而曰：「有無變通，不加賦而用足。」此劉晏制鹽之法也，而今之鹽利已無遺矣。况行之未善，則其害有甚
translation_en:
…the required tax payments are lighter than in other provinces, and are supplemented by revenue from salt. Yet both public and private resources are impoverished: this is something that I, your humble student, have indeed found puzzling. If it is attributed to the growth of population, since ancient times one has never heard of a numerous population being considered a calamity. If it is attributed to the spread of natural disasters, even the floods under Yao and the droughts under Tang did not bring such distress. As for the claim that diligence and frugality have declined while indolence and extravagance have spread, there is probably some truth in it. Yet diligence and frugality can be encouraged by example, and indolence and extravagance checked by admonition. The accumulated abuses of extortion and unpaid obligations probably also exist. Yet extortion can be investigated and arrears recovered.
Although I, your humble student, do not comprehend the plans for governing the realm, I know quite well the hidden sufferings of ordinary households. Once an unwarranted levy is imposed upon the prefectures and counties, the summonses and demands for payment leave even the chickens and dogs no peace. Repeated impositions amount to several times the regular taxes, and urgent collection is more oppressive still than ordinary tax enforcement. The rich are thereby impoverished, and the poor are utterly drained. Thus, at the first flood or drought, they can only flee or die. Yet we have never heard that these levies provision the frontier reserves, nor that they pay official salaries. Moreover, the people's wealth is limited. Once arbitrary levies multiply, regular taxes instead fall into arrears; how then can the state's resources avoid a shortfall? Thus, whenever an emergency arises, officials are helpless, without a plan. This is why public and private resources alike are exhausted. In my humble view, it is the result of arbitrary exactions and reckless spending.
You, sir, urgently wish to provide adequately for the state, and say: “Adjust the movement of resources between places of abundance and scarcity, so that expenditures are met without increasing taxes.” This is Liu Yan's method of regulating salt. Today, however, the revenue from salt has already been fully tapped. Moreover, if the method is poorly implemented, its harm may be greater…

title: 正德十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
於加賦不敢為國計取焉切於足民而曰
羸歉增减不歛民而備周此耿壽昌常平
之法也而今之社倉固虚庋矣况不得其
人則其害有甚於歛民不敢為吾民願焉
常觀吾山右之地雖爲山深谷無尺寸之
曠土地不遺利矣農工商賈各勤其業而
養不贍民無遺力矣復求理財之道豈能
天降而神輸哉惟望免其額外之取則吾
民雖困猶足以存生去夫不經之費則吾
===
省雖貧猶足以調度愚故以為用有常經
歛有常制今日之所急也大學傳曰生財
有大道生之者衆食之者寡為之者疾用
之者舒雖復千萬言蓋無以逾此孔子曰
不患寡而患不均不患貧而患不安則今
日之所患是有不專於財之之者而非愚
生之敢言也
punctuated:
於加賦，不敢為國計取焉。切於足民，而曰：「羸歉增减，不歛民而備周。」此耿壽昌常平之法也，而今之社倉固虚庋矣。况不得其人，則其害有甚於歛民，不敢為吾民願焉。

常觀吾山右之地，雖爲山深谷，無尺寸之曠土，地不遺利矣。農工商賈各勤其業，而養不贍，民無遺力矣。復求理財之道，豈能天降而神輸哉？惟望免其額外之取，則吾民雖困，猶足以存生；去夫不經之費，則吾省雖貧，猶足以調度。愚故以為，用有常經，歛有常制，今日之所急也。

《大學》傳曰：「生財有大道：生之者衆，食之者寡，為之者疾，用之者舒。」雖復千萬言，蓋無以逾此。孔子曰：「不患寡而患不均，不患貧而患不安。」則今日之所患，是有不專於財之之者，而非愚生之敢言也。
translation_en:
…than increasing taxes; I dare not adopt it as a measure for the state's finances. Concerned to provide adequately for the people, you say: “Adjust increases and reductions according to abundance and scarcity [?], so that reserves are sufficient without levying upon the people.” This is Geng Shouchang's ever-normal granary system. Yet our community granaries now stand empty. Moreover, if the right people are not appointed, its harm may exceed that of levying upon the people. I dare not wish this upon our people.

I have often observed that in our Shanyou—that is, Shanxi—despite its mountains and deep valleys [?], not an inch of land lies unused: the land yields all the benefit it can. Farmers, artisans, and merchants each labor diligently at their occupations, yet cannot adequately sustain themselves: the people exert all the strength they have. If we seek still further ways to manage wealth, can it descend from Heaven or be delivered by spirits? I hope only that exactions beyond the prescribed quotas may be remitted; then, though distressed, our people will still have enough to survive. Let irregular expenditures be eliminated; then, though poor, our province will still have enough to meet its needs. Thus, in my humble view, fixed rules for expenditure and established limits for levies are the urgent requirements of today.

The commentary to the Great Learning says: “There is a great way to produce wealth: let those who produce it be many and those who consume it few; let its production be swift and its expenditure slow.” Even ten million further words could scarcely improve upon this. Confucius said: “One should not worry about scarcity, but about unequal distribution; one should not worry about poverty, but about insecurity.” Thus, what ought to concern us today includes matters not exclusively concerned with wealth [?]; but these are not things that an ignorant student such as I dares to discuss.

title: 正德十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
山西鄉試錄後序
正德己卯秋八月山西鄉試
事竣錄成將以
獻〔世安〕謹序于末曰夫試士以
求才爲
國家用也初事御史誓於内外
之有職者曰敬玆
===
國典各盡厥責事隳才遺惟厥
愆及是則内外綱維終始明
肅監臨之責盡矣品式備舉
防範周嚴提調與監試之責
盡矣協心𨶒力庶務交脩凡
諸執事者之責盡矣〔世安〕輩
謬司文衡竭其不敏靜密以
punctuated:
山西鄉試錄後序

正德己卯秋八月，山西鄉試事竣，錄成，將以獻。〔世安〕謹序于末曰：夫試士以求才，爲國家用也。初事，御史誓於内外之有職者曰：「敬玆國典，各盡厥責。事隳才遺，惟厥愆。」及是，則内外綱維，終始明肅，監臨之責盡矣；品式備舉，防範周嚴，提調與監試之責盡矣；協心𨶒力，庶務交脩，凡諸執事者之責盡矣。〔世安〕輩謬司文衡，竭其不敏，靜密以
translation_en:
Afterword to the Record of the Shanxi Provincial Examination

In the eighth month of autumn in the jimao year of the Zhengde reign [1519], the Shanxi Provincial Examination was completed and its record compiled, ready for presentation to the throne. Shi'an 〔世安〕 respectfully appends this afterword: The purpose of examining scholars is to seek talent for service to the state. At the outset, the censor solemnly charged the officials serving inside and outside the examination compound: “Respect this great institution of the state, and let each fulfill his responsibilities. If the proceedings fail or talent is overlooked, the fault shall be yours.” Now, discipline within and without has been clear and strict from beginning to end: the Supervising Official has fulfilled his responsibilities. All prescribed procedures have been observed, and precautions have been comprehensive and rigorous: the Proctor and the Examination Inspector have fulfilled their responsibilities. Working with united purpose and combined strength [?], all concerned have attended to their various duties: everyone engaged in the proceedings has fulfilled his responsibilities. We, Shi'an 〔世安〕 and my colleagues, undeservedly entrusted with judging literary merit, have exerted our meager abilities, in quiet and close attention, to…

title: 正德十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
觀叅互以審猶反覆而後定
之亦少盡校文之責焉夫校
文以一日之長而欲以得士
之才難矣然文者言之精也
言者道之形也道者才之實
也茍有知言者豈不足以得
才乎哉山右古稱多才況今
===
密邇畿甸丕式最先而
聖化之漸涵已久故士爭自砥礪
以自見於時日盛而彬彬焉
今觀其文粹乎若皆深於道
也含欝吐發優乎若有諸躬
也鑿鑿乎古今得失其若達
於政也夫言由中出也固必
punctuated: 觀，叅互以審，猶反覆而後定之，亦少盡校文之責焉。夫校文以一日之長，而欲以得士之才，難矣。然文者，言之精也；言者，道之形也；道者，才之實也。茍有知言者，豈不足以得才乎哉？山右古稱多才，況今密邇畿甸，丕式最先，而聖化之漸涵已久，故士爭自砥礪，以自見於時，日盛而彬彬焉。今觀其文，粹乎若皆深於道也；含欝吐發，優乎若有諸躬也；鑿鑿乎古今得失，其若達於政也。夫言由中出也，固必
translation_en:
…to examine them, comparing and cross-checking to reach a considered judgment, yet reviewing them repeatedly before making a final decision: in this way we too have fulfilled, in some small measure, our responsibility for assessing the compositions. To assess compositions on the strength of a single day’s advantage in learning, hoping thereby to discover the candidates’ talents, is difficult indeed. Yet composition is the essence of speech; speech is the outward form of the Way; and the Way is the substance of talent. If there is someone who understands speech, would this not suffice to discover talent?

Shanyou has been renowned since antiquity for its abundance of talent. Moreover, it now lies close to the capital region, foremost in following the great model [?], and has long been steeped in the sage emperor’s transforming influence. Thus its scholars vie in honing themselves to make their abilities known in their own age, flourishing daily in cultivated refinement. Looking now at their compositions, their purity suggests that all are deeply versed in the Way. In what they hold within and express outwardly, their ease and amplitude suggest that they embody it in their own persons. Their precise treatment of successes and failures, ancient and modern, suggests an understanding of government. Since speech issues from within, there must assuredly…

title: 正德十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
有其實焉其末也又必有其
識焉識則可與進矣善用其
識則為明道為善治否則為
文奸為亂政諸士子登薦之
初終身之用基焉國家所以
求之者何如而自待者將奚
擇乎善利之間君子小人之
===
分天下治亂存亡之攸係其
幾微矣以識取之而實則違
豈獨取之者之責哉夫有其
識而不為僞也為之不力不
勇也識以明之誠以居之勇
以行之致於道以達於政斯
謂之才斯無負於今日之求
punctuated: 有其實焉，其末也，又必有其識焉。識則可與進矣。善用其識，則為明道，為善治；否則為文奸，為亂政。諸士子登薦之初，終身之用基焉。國家所以求之者何如，而自待者將奚擇乎？善利之間，君子小人之分，天下治亂存亡之攸係，其幾微矣！以識取之，而實則違，豈獨取之者之責哉？夫有其識而不為，僞也；為之不力，不勇也。識以明之，誠以居之，勇以行之，致於道以達於政，斯謂之才，斯無負於今日之求
translation_en: …there must be substance behind it; in its ultimate expression [?], there must also be discernment. Those possessing discernment may be advanced. If they use their discernment well, they will illuminate the Way and bring about good government; otherwise, they will practise deceit through writing and throw government into disorder. When these scholars first gain recommendation, the foundation is laid for their lifelong service. What does the state seek from them, and what will they choose as the standard they set for themselves? Between goodness and personal gain lies the distinction between the gentleman and the petty man; upon it depend the order or disorder, survival or destruction of the realm. How subtle is the point at which they diverge! If men are selected for their discernment but their actual conduct runs counter to it, can responsibility rest solely with those who selected them? To possess discernment yet fail to act is hypocrisy; to act without exerting oneself is a lack of courage. Use discernment to understand, sincerity to abide by that understanding, and courage to put it into practice. Attain the Way and apply it to government: this is what may be called talent, and this is how one may prove worthy of today's search for such men…

title: 正德十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
與他日之用矣此諸士子之
責也所自盡也竊有望焉
江西饒州府鄱陽縣儒學教
諭成世安謹序
punctuated:
與他日之用矣。此諸士子之責也，所自盡也，竊有望焉。
江西饒州府鄱陽縣儒學教諭成世安謹序。
translation_en:
…and their employment in days to come. This is the responsibility of all you examination candidates, in which you must exert yourselves to the utmost. I humbly place my hopes in you.
Preface respectfully composed by Cheng Shi’an, Instructor of the Confucian School of Poyang County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi.
